119	### Core Rules
120	
121	Rule ids are `LY-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section); acceptance criteria are `AC-n`. Every table below carries an **Owner** column or states its owner in the lead-in: Layout's own tables hold only identity, tiles, rectangles, sockets, hardpoints, slots, anchors, membership, offsets, welds and counters. Locked constants and formulas from the kernel, the Graph, the Controller and the Pipeline are used by name with their registry values and are never restated differently (a needed different value would be a CONFLICT line in Open Questions, never a new number). Provisional contracts with undesigned or in-flight systems are marked **(provisional — <system> undesigned)**. Conflicts, clarifications and asks are marked **CONFLICT**, **CLARIFY** and **ASK**; they are routed in Cross-References and Open Questions, never silently resolved in a neighbour's text.
122	
123	#### 1.1 Block, ownership and data kinds
124	
125	**LY-1 — One block, one ownership clause.** Layout registers exactly one state block, `layout.state` (registry: `layout_state_block`), in the kernel's block registry (CR-8):
126	
127	| Field | Value | Owner |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| `block_id` | `layout.state` | Layout |
130	| `owner` | Layout | Layout |
131	| `class` | `SIM` | Layout |
132	| `persist` / `persist_scope` | true / `WORLD` | Layout |
133	| `scope` | `SHARED` | Layout |
134	| `repl_hint` | `SHARED_SUMMARY` — the summary IS the instance table plus the `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` values *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the single `template_hash` is split, LY-26 e)*; geometry never travels, because templates are identical on every client by catalogue version | Layout |
135	| `schema_version` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 | Layout |
136	| `restore_after` | `[]` — Layout is the root of the restore order; it reads no other block in `restore()` | Layout |
137	| Hooks | exactly one: `layout.doors` (LY-10) | Layout |
138	| Callbacks | `snapshot()`, `restore(data, stored_version)`, `default_state()`, `post_restore()`, `read_view()` (kernel CR-8 descriptor) | Layout |
139	
140	The ownership clause routed from the Graph (LS-6, LSG:74; LSG:1158 Open Question 9 requires it "repeated verbatim in the Layout and Interaction GDDs") is, word for word: "**Layout owns** room identity, polygon, `V` (tiles) and `exposed_tiles`; the Graph caches `V` and `exposed_tiles` as derived fields (not hashed; rebuilt in `post_restore`, which is why `restore_after: [layout.state]`). **The Graph owns** the atmosphere — `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `T`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle_ml` — and every opening/hatch `area` and `door_state`, every VALVE `open` and every breaker `closed`; Interaction issues the commands, the Graph publishes the mutators (R11; one writer per fact, kernel H3)." Layout's side of the same clause: **sections own compartment/room GEOMETRY and the volume `V` in tiles; the Graph owns atmosphere and node/edge state; Layout only PROJECTS `area` into a rectangle (LY-9).** The Graph's block `graph.state` is registered with `restore_after: [layout.state]` (LSG:64, LSG:1023) and the Emitter's `emitter.state` with `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` (EM:104); this rule is the other end of both edges. Entity ids are allocated by the owning block from a counter stored in it (CR-8): Layout owns the section, body and room counters (LY-6).
141	
142	**LY-2 — Templates are static; instances are state.** A **template** is authored, immutable, integer-only data: rooms, wall runs, kit-piece placements, doors, sockets, hardpoints, plate positions, loose and story slots, anchors and fixture anchors (LY-4). It lives under `assets/data/sections/`, is loaded and range-checked in BOOTING (every JSON number is converted with an explicit integer cast and bound check, because the engine's JSON parser returns floats [UNV] (NOT SOURCEABLE: `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` has no scripting or core file) — the same defensive pattern the Graph and the Item DB use), and is **never in a snapshot**. An **instance** is a row in `layout.state` that names a template. The block therefore stores instances *by reference*: full geometry in the block would bloat it (rectangles × sections), duplicate authored data, defeat the Vertical Slice "seed plus deltas" model, and let an exporter bug corrupt the world permanently; a second `layout.templates` block would add a second restore root for no gain. Both are rejected. (→ ADR-LAY-01.) A template edit between builds is handled like an Item DB `def_id` change: by `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` and the drift policy of LY-26 e. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Catalogue loading in an export build** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: in a Godot export, non-resource files such as `assets/data/**/*.json` are dropped unless the export filters list them, and a `DirAccess` scan returns entries in a platform-dependent order, so a directory-scanned catalogue can pass in the editor and fail (or reorder) in a release build. The catalogue is therefore built from a **committed manifest** (`assets/data/sections/manifest.json`, one `template_id` and path per line) **loaded in sorted `template_id` order**, never from a directory scan; the four MVP template paths (`home_ship`, `derelict_a`, `derelict_b`, `pod`) and `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` are added to the export filter (`include_filter` for `*.json`); and an **exported-build smoke check** loads all four MVP templates from the exported package and compares the resulting `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` with the editor run (AC-178).
143	
144	| Data kind | Lives in | Written by | Persisted | Owner |
145	|---|---|---|---|---|
146	| Template (rooms, tile sets, rect table, doors, sockets, hardpoints, plates, slots, anchors) | `assets/data/sections/*.json`, loaded at BOOTING | authors and the offline tool; never at runtime | no | Layout (schema, structural lint); Derelict Authoring (authored files, content lint) |
147	| Bodies table: `{body_id, origin_section_id, state LIVE\|DISSOLVED}` | `layout.state` | LM1-LM4 | yes | Layout |
148	| Section-instance table: `{section_id, template_id, geometry_hash, visual_hash, body_id, offset_px (two ints), rot_q (0), room_id_base, graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}, discarded}` (13 ints per row, D.21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `template_hash` split into the two u32 hashes of LY-26 e)* | `layout.state` | LM1, LM4 | yes | Layout |
149	| Socket-state table (sparse, non-`FREE` only): `{section_id, socket_index, state, seam_id}` | `layout.state` | LM2, LM3 | yes | Layout |
150	| Weld history `welds[]`: `{seam_id, section_a, socket_a, section_b, socket_b, welded_at_T, state ACTIVE\|CUT_SEALED\|CUT_RAGGED, cut_at_T}` | `layout.state` | LM2, LM3 | yes | Layout (the `seam_id` is the Graph's; Layout allocates none) |
151	| Counters `next_section_id`, `next_body_id`, `next_room_id` | `layout.state` | LM1 | yes | Layout |
152	| Derived caches: broadphase grid, door-leaf rects, variant-slot activity, `version` / `static_version` / `leaf_version(section_id)`, `graph_ref` lookup maps, `opening_leaves` (edge id → leaf slots) | RAM | LM1-LM4, `layout.doors`, `restore` | **never** | Layout (PROJECTOR objects: the PROJECTOR) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
153	
154	**LY-3 — Units, grid, frames and transforms (stated once).**
155	(a) *Integers only.* The unit is the base pixel; `TILE_PX` 48 is the floor tile; the half-tile grid is 24 px (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 is the wall depth). No float exists anywhere in the module. Every footprint coordinate lies on the 24-px grid, with the single exception of the moving edge of a DOOR_LEAF rectangle (LY-7).
156	(b) *Frames.* A **section-local** frame has its origin at the section's grid origin; local coordinates are `>= 0` by authoring. The **body frame** is the section-local frame plus `offset_px(section_id)`. Layout has no world frame (Body's pose and the Pipeline's camera are not Layout's).
157	(c) *One rule for which frame a read answers in.* Every Layout geometry read returns SECTION-LOCAL base px (fixture anchors EM:331; `anchor_geometry.base_px_polyline[]` and `room_surface` FT:306; hardpoint, slot and socket anchors); the caller composes `section_offset(section_id)` (FT:306 "the section's body-frame offset"). The reads that answer for one body answer in the BODY frame: `OccluderSource.rects_in` and `solid_in`, because the sweep (PCI:103, "`pos` base px, body frame") and the occlusion test (EM-30, EM:253) run there, and the body-frame helpers built on them or on the offsets — `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `section_at`, `weld_offset` and `detach_preview` (LY-28).
158	(d) *Transforms are integer translation only.* A section's `offset_px` lies on the 24-px grid (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`) — a DERIVED property of D.6 and D.12 over `GRID_24`-linted inputs, never an input constraint; a reserved `rot_q` field is stored and **must be 0** (the template lint and `restore` reject any other value with `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`); there is no mirror. Variety comes from authored socket FACINGS (LY-13), not from rotating a section. Rejected: four-way rotation (the kit's wall faces are authored for the up-screen convention only, PIPE:794; the art bible's "× 2 orientations" is pipes only) and free transform (the anti-pillar). A detached section "translates without rotation in the interior view" (PIPE:694).
159	(e) *Zoom invariance.* No `k`, `s`, `field_h` or zoom value appears anywhere in Layout (FT-34): every length, clearance and rectangle is base px and identical at every ladder step, so there is nothing to re-check when the zoom ladder changes (the reflexion-log pattern "an invariant written against 'the default' must be re-checked whenever a later decision adds reachable states" is satisfied by construction).
160	(f) *Floor division.* Body-frame coordinates and `offset_px` may be negative after a detach re-base, so every px-to-tile conversion is FLOOR division (D.1); truncating integer division is forbidden.
161	
162	**LY-4 — Template schema (field by field, mapped to the art-bible kit).** `SECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1. The art bible's room kit (6.3 "The room kit: what one kit must contain") is the authoring input: Derelict Authoring and the Vertical Slice procedural generator consume this schema (LSG, IDX:28).

180	
181	Schema ownership: **Layout owns the schema and the structural lint (LY-30); Derelict Authoring owns the authored files, the content and visual-rule lint, and the kit pieces** *(provisional — Derelict Authoring undesigned)*.
182	*The `pod` template (answers Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-17 and Web Map ASK-L1 for Layout's part).* `pod_cabin` (one room, 2 × 2 tiles, `V` 4 — exactly `ROOM_TILES_MIN`, inclusive, so `V_RANGE` passes) is an ordinary template under schema v1: Layout adds no pod record type and persists no section kind; the `kind` argument forwarded to M1 comes from the Graph's LS-17 enum, and which value the pod receives is the Graph's and Web Map's call (OQ-26). A template with exactly one room is exempt from `ROOM_NO_EXIT` and `CLEAR_PATH_BLOCKED` (its one room is its `entry_room_key`, and the pod is entered and left by Web Map's pod hop, never by walking through a door); `ROOM_UNREACHABLE` passes trivially. Layout's structural lint has no fixture minimum — `FIXTURE_COUNT_ROOM` is Authoring's CONTENT lint (LY-30) — so the `fixtures_min` exemption is Authoring's to write and Layout grants nothing. A pod room that hosts no HULL_SEGMENT is not tagged `outer`, so `OUTER_ROOM_HULL_RUNS` does not apply.
183	
184	**LY-5 — A room is a rectilinear, 4-connected set of floor tiles on the 24-px lattice.** `room.tiles[]` is the list of floor tiles of one room, each a 48×48 square whose section-local origin is `origin_px + 48 × (tx, ty)`, sorted row-major (`ty` ascending, then `tx` ascending). A tile's **tile id** is its index in that list. `V = |tiles|` (D.3). A room is 4-connected (neighbours differ by exactly one in `tx` or `ty`), has no interior holes and no diagonal pinch vertex (lint `ROOM_SHAPE`), has `V` within the Graph's compartment bounds (`ROOM_TILES_MIN`..`ROOM_TILES_MAX`, 4-200, LSG:299 — cited, not redefined) and belongs to exactly one section (LSG:172 "a compartment belongs to one section"). L-shapes are allowed; two rooms of a section never share a tile. The "polygon" the Graph names (LSG:74, LSG:849) is DERIVED: `room_boundary(room_id)` returns the closed boundary polyline (unit edges traced clockwise from the north-west corner of the minimum-id tile), never stored. `room_surface(compartment_id).floor_tiles[]` is literally the sorted tile list in section-local px (tile origin), so the Failure & Trail ordering "(distance from the anchor, tile id)" (FT:383) has a defined tie-break.
185	*(orchestrator ruling: the floor-tile lattice.)* A wall between two rooms is ONE 24-px footprint strip (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24; Pipeline D.12's own example — wall rows `[240, 264)`, first legal row 264 — presumes exactly this), so the floor on its far side begins 24 px later than a 48-px lattice would put it: **tile parity flips across every shared wall**. Each room therefore carries its own `origin_px` on the 24-px grid and its tiles are counted in 48-px units from that origin. This is a storage-unit refinement of "tiles on the 48-px grid", not a new tile size: `TILE_PX` stays 48, `V` is unchanged, and the alternatives are rejected — a double wall between rooms (a 48-px-thick shared wall needs two door frames in line and two Graph openings per passage, or a 48-deep frame the art bible does not define) and a full-48 wall row with a 24-px walkable skirt owned by no tile. The **sill** — the door-width × 24-px floor strip inside a doorway — is not a tile and does not count in `V`: each door declares a `sill_room` (one of its two flanking rooms) and `room_at(section_id, px)` answers `sill_room` for a px on the sill, so there is no walkable point in a section where `room_at` answers `NONE`.
186	
187	**LY-6 — Identity, allocation and the migration stance.**
188	(a) *Ids.* Layout allocates `section_id` from `next_section_id`, `body_id` from `next_body_id` and `room_id` (a u32) from `next_room_id` **in template room order at `build_section`**, contiguous per instance (`room_id = room_id_base + room_index`). Ids are never reused and never renumbered (the Graph's append-only pattern, LS-15). A discarded section keeps its row as a tombstone (LY-19), so its ids stay consumed.
189	(b) *Keys.* Template-local keys (`room_key`, `socket_key`, `hp_key`, `door_key`, `node_ref`, `edge_ref`) are strings used for lint, diagnostics, migration and restore verification. The block persists only numeric ids, socket ordinals and the `template_id` string.
190	(c) *Graph ids.* The Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids from its own `next_*` counters in template order (LSG:170, LSG:180). Layout persists, per instance, `graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` so a template-local `node_ref` / `edge_ref` index maps to a numeric Graph id by `base + index` and a compartment id maps to its room by `comp_base`, deterministically. The seam id in `welds[]` is the Graph's `seam_id` (LSG:72 SeamRecord); Layout allocates no seam id.
191	(d) **ANSWERED by the Graph (LS-15, LS-19, M1 row; *Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass*); the ask is closed (OQ-4).** M1 `instantiate_section(section_id, template_id, kind)` takes a caller section id and now returns `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`, which Layout stores as `graph_ref_base`; M1 advances the Graph's persisted `next_section_id` to `max(section_id) + 1`, so Layout allocates the section id and the Graph's counter follows it. `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}` and `seam_view(seam_id)` is a pure read of `{state, sub_edges[], leak_bp, opening_ids[]}`; Layout uses `opening_ids[]` for the mated-hatch leaf map (LY-11, LY-16). The only mismatch case left is the restore-time guard of Edge Cases ("Save, restore and drift"). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
192	(e) *Migration stance, stated here and again in Open Questions:* "A renamed `room_key` or `template_id` needs a migration step in the owner once the first build has been given outside the project (SL-14, SL:219); before that, saves are disposable (SL-14)." This closes Save/Load Open Question 12 (SL:1300) and the Graph's Open Question 9 (LSG:1158) from the Layout side. Because the persisted ids are numeric and assigned at build, a template that merely *reorders* rooms changes ids only for NEW instances; existing saves keep theirs.
193	
194	#### 1.2 Rectangles, walls, frames
195	
196	**LY-7 — The footprint rectangle record and flags** (registry: `layout_rect_flags`)**.** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, stored as packed integer arrays plus one flags byte, **half-open** `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` over pixel CELLS (the tile grid, the foot box and sprite rows are all cells). Flags: `SOLID` (blocks `LocomotionStep`), `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` (the Emitter's `occludes_light`, EM-20), `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL`. Rects are SIMULATION DATA (kernel H10): never read back from the scene tree, never produced by an engine physics shape, and the avatar has no physics body. Layout never calls its own rects "collision shapes" (wording refresh routed in Cross-References). The only legal flag combinations (anything else is the lint error `RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`):
197	
198	| Class | SOLID | OCCLUDES_LIGHT | DOOR_LEAF | PROP | MACHINE | HULL | Notes |
199	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
200	| Wall run | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/1 | HULL on exterior-facing runs |
201	| Door jamb | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | fixed, either side of the gap |
202	| Door leaf | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | always solid and occluding (no glass in MVP, EM-20); dynamic (LY-9) |
203	| Socket hatch plate (variant slot PLATE) while `FREE`, `CAPPED`, `CUT_OPEN` or `WELDED` one-sided | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | the plate covers the whole socket span (`width_tiles × 48` × 24); a reserved variant slot, not a static rect (LY-15). While `CUT_OPEN` it is solid AND occluding: nothing lies beyond a cut, and no avatar can leave the hull through it. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
204	| Socket jamb (variant slot JAMB), `WELDED` two-sided, `width_tiles >= 3` only | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | the hull bulkhead beside the 96-px hatch doorway, `(width_tiles × 48 − 96)` × 24; exterior hull wall, hence HULL; zero-width (omitted) at `width_tiles` 2. Same precedent as the hull-port row below: the HULL run compiles in parts with no SOLID overlap. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
205	| Tall prop / machinery node | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0/1 | 0 | `occludes_light` authored |
206	| Low prop | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | blocks feet, not light |
207	| Hull port (`wall_port` piece in a HULL run; routed from Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-19 / OQ-V2) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | blocks feet, passes light, so a residual lamp's light truthfully leaves the hull; its footprint replaces the HULL run's own over its span (the run compiles in two parts, no SOLID overlap) and `CONTAINMENT_LEAK` is unaffected because it is SOLID; it is absent from `rects_in`, not a translucent occluder, so EM-20 (f) is untouched |

### Core Rules

Rule ids are `LY-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section); acceptance criteria are `AC-n`. Every table below carries an **Owner** column or states its owner in the lead-in: Layout's own tables hold only identity, tiles, rectangles, sockets, hardpoints, slots, anchors, membership, offsets, welds and counters. Locked constants and formulas from the kernel, the Graph, the Controller and the Pipeline are used by name with their registry values and are never restated differently (a needed different value would be a CONFLICT line in Open Questions, never a new number). Provisional contracts with undesigned or in-flight systems are marked **(provisional — <system> undesigned)**. Conflicts, clarifications and asks are marked **CONFLICT**, **CLARIFY** and **ASK**; they are routed in Cross-References and Open Questions, never silently resolved in a neighbour's text.

#### 1.1 Block, ownership and data kinds

**LY-1 — One block, one ownership clause.** Layout registers exactly one state block, `layout.state` (registry: `layout_state_block`), in the kernel's block registry (CR-8):

| Field | Value | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | `layout.state` | Layout |
| `owner` | Layout | Layout |
| `class` | `SIM` | Layout |
| `persist` / `persist_scope` | true / `WORLD` | Layout |
| `scope` | `SHARED` | Layout |
| `repl_hint` | `SHARED_SUMMARY` — the summary IS the instance table plus the `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` values *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the single `template_hash` is split, LY-26 e)*; geometry never travels, because templates are identical on every client by catalogue version | Layout |
| `schema_version` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 | Layout |
| `restore_after` | `[]` — Layout is the root of the restore order; it reads no other block in `restore()` | Layout |
| Hooks | exactly one: `layout.doors` (LY-10) | Layout |
| Callbacks | `snapshot()`, `restore(data, stored_version)`, `default_state()`, `post_restore()`, `read_view()` (kernel CR-8 descriptor) | Layout |

The ownership clause routed from the Graph (LS-6, LSG:74; LSG:1158 Open Question 9 requires it "repeated verbatim in the Layout and Interaction GDDs") is, word for word: "**Layout owns** room identity, polygon, `V` (tiles) and `exposed_tiles`; the Graph caches `V` and `exposed_tiles` as derived fields (not hashed; rebuilt in `post_restore`, which is why `restore_after: [layout.state]`). **The Graph owns** the atmosphere — `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `T`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle_ml` — and every opening/hatch `area` and `door_state`, every VALVE `open` and every breaker `closed`; Interaction issues the commands, the Graph publishes the mutators (R11; one writer per fact, kernel H3)." Layout's side of the same clause: **sections own compartment/room GEOMETRY and the volume `V` in tiles; the Graph owns atmosphere and node/edge state; Layout only PROJECTS `area` into a rectangle (LY-9).** The Graph's block `graph.state` is registered with `restore_after: [layout.state]` (LSG:64, LSG:1023) and the Emitter's `emitter.state` with `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` (EM:104); this rule is the other end of both edges. Entity ids are allocated by the owning block from a counter stored in it (CR-8): Layout owns the section, body and room counters (LY-6).

**LY-2 — Templates are static; instances are state.** A **template** is authored, immutable, integer-only data: rooms, wall runs, kit-piece placements, doors, sockets, hardpoints, plate positions, loose and story slots, anchors and fixture anchors (LY-4). It lives under `assets/data/sections/`, is loaded and range-checked in BOOTING (every JSON number is converted with an explicit integer cast and bound check, because the engine's JSON parser returns floats [UNV] (NOT SOURCEABLE: `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` has no scripting or core file) — the same defensive pattern the Graph and the Item DB use), and is **never in a snapshot**. An **instance** is a row in `layout.state` that names a template. The block therefore stores instances *by reference*: full geometry in the block would bloat it (rectangles × sections), duplicate authored data, defeat the Vertical Slice "seed plus deltas" model, and let an exporter bug corrupt the world permanently; a second `layout.templates` block would add a second restore root for no gain. Both are rejected. (→ ADR-LAY-01.) A template edit between builds is handled like an Item DB `def_id` change: by `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` and the drift policy of LY-26 e. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Catalogue loading in an export build** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: in a Godot export, non-resource files such as `assets/data/**/*.json` are dropped unless the export filters list them, and a `DirAccess` scan returns entries in a platform-dependent order, so a directory-scanned catalogue can pass in the editor and fail (or reorder) in a release build. The catalogue is therefore built from a **committed manifest** (`assets/data/sections/manifest.json`, one `template_id` and path per line) **loaded in sorted `template_id` order**, never from a directory scan; the four MVP template paths (`home_ship`, `derelict_a`, `derelict_b`, `pod`) and `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` are added to the export filter (`include_filter` for `*.json`); and an **exported-build smoke check** loads all four MVP templates from the exported package and compares the resulting `geometry_hash` / `visual_hash` with the editor run (AC-178).

| Data kind | Lives in | Written by | Persisted | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Template (rooms, tile sets, rect table, doors, sockets, hardpoints, plates, slots, anchors) | `assets/data/sections/*.json`, loaded at BOOTING | authors and the offline tool; never at runtime | no | Layout (schema, structural lint); Derelict Authoring (authored files, content lint) |
| Bodies table: `{body_id, origin_section_id, state LIVE\|DISSOLVED}` | `layout.state` | LM1-LM4 | yes | Layout |
| Section-instance table: `{section_id, template_id, geometry_hash, visual_hash, body_id, offset_px (two ints), rot_q (0), room_id_base, graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}, discarded}` (13 ints per row, D.21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `template_hash` split into the two u32 hashes of LY-26 e)* | `layout.state` | LM1, LM4 | yes | Layout |
| Socket-state table (sparse, non-`FREE` only): `{section_id, socket_index, state, seam_id}` | `layout.state` | LM2, LM3 | yes | Layout |
| Weld history `welds[]`: `{seam_id, section_a, socket_a, section_b, socket_b, welded_at_T, state ACTIVE\|CUT_SEALED\|CUT_RAGGED, cut_at_T}` | `layout.state` | LM2, LM3 | yes | Layout (the `seam_id` is the Graph's; Layout allocates none) |
| Counters `next_section_id`, `next_body_id`, `next_room_id` | `layout.state` | LM1 | yes | Layout |
| Derived caches: broadphase grid, door-leaf rects, variant-slot activity, `version` / `static_version` / `leaf_version(section_id)`, `graph_ref` lookup maps, `opening_leaves` (edge id → leaf slots) | RAM | LM1-LM4, `layout.doors`, `restore` | **never** | Layout (PROJECTOR objects: the PROJECTOR) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

**LY-3 — Units, grid, frames and transforms (stated once).**
(a) *Integers only.* The unit is the base pixel; `TILE_PX` 48 is the floor tile; the half-tile grid is 24 px (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 is the wall depth). No float exists anywhere in the module. Every footprint coordinate lies on the 24-px grid, with the single exception of the moving edge of a DOOR_LEAF rectangle (LY-7).
(b) *Frames.* A **section-local** frame has its origin at the section's grid origin; local coordinates are `>= 0` by authoring. The **body frame** is the section-local frame plus `offset_px(section_id)`. Layout has no world frame (Body's pose and the Pipeline's camera are not Layout's).
(c) *One rule for which frame a read answers in.* Every Layout geometry read returns SECTION-LOCAL base px (fixture anchors EM:331; `anchor_geometry.base_px_polyline[]` and `room_surface` FT:306; hardpoint, slot and socket anchors); the caller composes `section_offset(section_id)` (FT:306 "the section's body-frame offset"). The reads that answer for one body answer in the BODY frame: `OccluderSource.rects_in` and `solid_in`, because the sweep (PCI:103, "`pos` base px, body frame") and the occlusion test (EM-30, EM:253) run there, and the body-frame helpers built on them or on the offsets — `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `section_at`, `weld_offset` and `detach_preview` (LY-28).
(d) *Transforms are integer translation only.* A section's `offset_px` lies on the 24-px grid (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`) — a DERIVED property of D.6 and D.12 over `GRID_24`-linted inputs, never an input constraint; a reserved `rot_q` field is stored and **must be 0** (the template lint and `restore` reject any other value with `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`); there is no mirror. Variety comes from authored socket FACINGS (LY-13), not from rotating a section. Rejected: four-way rotation (the kit's wall faces are authored for the up-screen convention only, PIPE:794; the art bible's "× 2 orientations" is pipes only) and free transform (the anti-pillar). A detached section "translates without rotation in the interior view" (PIPE:694).
(e) *Zoom invariance.* No `k`, `s`, `field_h` or zoom value appears anywhere in Layout (FT-34): every length, clearance and rectangle is base px and identical at every ladder step, so there is nothing to re-check when the zoom ladder changes (the reflexion-log pattern "an invariant written against 'the default' must be re-checked whenever a later decision adds reachable states" is satisfied by construction).
(f) *Floor division.* Body-frame coordinates and `offset_px` may be negative after a detach re-base, so every px-to-tile conversion is FLOOR division (D.1); truncating integer division is forbidden.

**LY-4 — Template schema (field by field, mapped to the art-bible kit).** `SECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1. The art bible's room kit (6.3 "The room kit: what one kit must contain") is the authoring input: Derelict Authoring and the Vertical Slice procedural generator consume this schema (LSG, IDX:28).

| Record | Fields | Kit piece / source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Header | `template_id` (snake_case, unique), `schema`, `dialect` (`foundry`/`lattice`/`civil`; every MVP template is `foundry`, IDB), `kind_default`, `size_tiles {w, h}`, `entry_room_key` (the room the pod arrives in, one meaning across all templates: the pod-dock room `airlock` for the home ship, `a_dock` for derelict A, `b_dock` for derelict B; registry `mvp_template_roster`) | dialect set, art bible 3.3 | `w <= SECTION_MAX_TILES_W`, `h <= SECTION_MAX_TILES_H`; `kind_default` is a convenience, the build call passes `kind` explicitly |
| Room | `room_key` (snake_case, unique in the template), `room_type` (lint hint), `outer` (bool), `frame_exception` (bool), `origin_px {x, y}` (on the 24 grid), `tile_runs[] {ty, tx0, tx1}` (inclusive row spans in 48-px tile units from `origin_px`) | floor (base, variant, threshold) | expanded to the sorted tile list (LY-5) |
| Wall run | `run_id` (template-local int), `orientation EW\|NS`, `start_px {x, y}` (24 grid), `len_tiles`, `kind HULL\|PARTITION`, `room_key_a`, `room_key_b` (or `EXTERIOR`), `face_h_px` (default 72, art bible 8.2 front face), `face_variant FACE\|CAP_ONLY` (default `FACE`; a HULL run on a room's south edge must be `CAP_ONLY`, D.14) | wall straight face, inner/outer corner, end cap, top cap | footprint = the 24-px strip (LY-8); HULL runs feed `exposed_tiles` (counted on the authored run, before the socket-span split of LY-15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Kit placement | `kit_piece_id`, `px` or tile, `layer`, `footprint {x0, y0, x1, y1}` (copied from the kit piece), `flags` | every placed piece | the authored footprint rect travels with the kit piece; Layout lints alignment |
| Rect | `idx` (template-local, dense from 0), `x0, y0, x1, y1` (half-open), `flags` (LY-7), `owner_kind`, `owner_ref` | derived from wall runs and kit placements at template load | the stored table is the compiled result; `idx` is the stable rect id (D.9). The compiled `idx` space has three parts: static rects (sorted), then one reserved leaf slot per door, then two reserved variant slots (PLATE, JAMB) per hatched socket — the HULL run containing a socket span is split into before / span / after and the span is owned by the socket's variant slots (LY-15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Door | `door_key`, `wall_run_id`, `doorway_start_px` (for a socket hatch derived: it equals the socket's `start_px`, low-aligned, LY-14 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), `width_px` (96, art bible 8.2 door cell), `hinge LOW\|HIGH` (interior doors only; a socket hatch's hinge is fixed by LY-9), `sill_room_key`, `edge_ref` (the Graph template OPENING) or `hatch_socket_key`, `area_max`, `door_motor_node_ref` (IDB Open Question 2), `leaf_rect_idx` | door frame + leaf (closed / open / cut / welded, art bible 6.5) | the leaf rect index is reserved even while the leaf is absent (D.9) |
| Socket | `socket_key`, `facing N\|E\|S\|W`, `line_px` (outer face of the hull wall), `start_px` (along the run), `width_tiles` (1-12), `class_id`, `lanes[] {loop, lane_index, node_ref, port_local_index}`, `hatch {door_key}` or none | port shape inherits the donor dialect (art bible 3.3) | LY-13 |
| Hardpoint | `hp_key`, `node_ref`, `room_key`, `accepted_kinds[]`, `ports[]` (ordered port-type ids, `<= MAX_PORTS_PER_DEF` 8), `accepted_subtypes[]`, `cell`, `anchor_px`, `mount WALL_FACE\|FLOOR`, `host_face` or floor tile, `footprint_rect_idx`, `socket_tag` (advisory) | machinery node (96×96) incl. the hull-plate module position | LY-20 |
| Plate position | `segment_key`, `node_ref`, `wall_run_id`, `start_tile`, `len_tiles`, `bound_room_key` | hull plate module | LY-21 |
| Loose slot | `slot_id`, `room_key`, `anchor_px`, `surface FLOOR\|SHELF\|CRATE`, `allowed_class[]`, `capacity` 1 | props 8-10 | LY-22 |
| Story slot | `slot_id`, `role CAUSE\|VERB\|ABSENCE`, `room_key`, `anchor_px` | storytelling set (Vertical Slice; art bible 6.5 ("one cause, one verb, one absence per wreck", placed as three tagged slots)) | list reserved, empty in MVP |
| Anchor | `anchor_key`, `ref {node_ref, port_local_index} \| {edge_ref}`, `kind WALL_FACE\|FLOOR`, `host_face`, `polyline[] {x, y}`, `max_sev_class` (input from the Graph descriptor data; Layout never reads severity) | pipe mount, light fixture | LY-23 |
| Fixture anchor | `local_id`, `kind`, `anchor_px`, `shape_id`, `base_pm`, `node_ref`, `hue_class` (the EM:328 placement record) | light fixture | `shape_id`, `base_pm`, `hue_class` come from the installed def's `emits` (IDB); Layout carries the placement |
| Instrument placement *(provisional — routed from In-World Instruments IW-31)* | `instrument_id` (a key into `assets/data/instruments/`), `node_ref` or `room_key` plus `quantity` (the Graph binding, carried opaquely: Layout never reads a quantity), `mount WALL_FACE\|MACHINE_PANEL`, `host_face`, `anchor_px` | a `Kit placement` of category `mach` or `prop` (gauge, dial, sight-glass) | exposed through `subject_anchors(section_id)` with `kind_hint` `INSTRUMENT` (LY-23) so Interaction registers the subject; `INSTRUMENT_NO_BINDING`, the at-least-3-eligible-surfaces floor and the DIAL_L placement constraint (46 of 48 rows: never a console-face detail inside a cap-plus-face prop) are Derelict Authoring's CONTENT lint, not Layout's |

Schema ownership: **Layout owns the schema and the structural lint (LY-30); Derelict Authoring owns the authored files, the content and visual-rule lint, and the kit pieces** *(provisional — Derelict Authoring undesigned)*.
*The `pod` template (answers Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-17 and Web Map ASK-L1 for Layout's part).* `pod_cabin` (one room, 2 × 2 tiles, `V` 4 — exactly `ROOM_TILES_MIN`, inclusive, so `V_RANGE` passes) is an ordinary template under schema v1: Layout adds no pod record type and persists no section kind; the `kind` argument forwarded to M1 comes from the Graph's LS-17 enum, and which value the pod receives is the Graph's and Web Map's call (OQ-26). A template with exactly one room is exempt from `ROOM_NO_EXIT` and `CLEAR_PATH_BLOCKED` (its one room is its `entry_room_key`, and the pod is entered and left by Web Map's pod hop, never by walking through a door); `ROOM_UNREACHABLE` passes trivially. Layout's structural lint has no fixture minimum — `FIXTURE_COUNT_ROOM` is Authoring's CONTENT lint (LY-30) — so the `fixtures_min` exemption is Authoring's to write and Layout grants nothing. A pod room that hosts no HULL_SEGMENT is not tagged `outer`, so `OUTER_ROOM_HULL_RUNS` does not apply.

**LY-5 — A room is a rectilinear, 4-connected set of floor tiles on the 24-px lattice.** `room.tiles[]` is the list of floor tiles of one room, each a 48×48 square whose section-local origin is `origin_px + 48 × (tx, ty)`, sorted row-major (`ty` ascending, then `tx` ascending). A tile's **tile id** is its index in that list. `V = |tiles|` (D.3). A room is 4-connected (neighbours differ by exactly one in `tx` or `ty`), has no interior holes and no diagonal pinch vertex (lint `ROOM_SHAPE`), has `V` within the Graph's compartment bounds (`ROOM_TILES_MIN`..`ROOM_TILES_MAX`, 4-200, LSG:299 — cited, not redefined) and belongs to exactly one section (LSG:172 "a compartment belongs to one section"). L-shapes are allowed; two rooms of a section never share a tile. The "polygon" the Graph names (LSG:74, LSG:849) is DERIVED: `room_boundary(room_id)` returns the closed boundary polyline (unit edges traced clockwise from the north-west corner of the minimum-id tile), never stored. `room_surface(compartment_id).floor_tiles[]` is literally the sorted tile list in section-local px (tile origin), so the Failure & Trail ordering "(distance from the anchor, tile id)" (FT:383) has a defined tie-break.
*(orchestrator ruling: the floor-tile lattice.)* A wall between two rooms is ONE 24-px footprint strip (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24; Pipeline D.12's own example — wall rows `[240, 264)`, first legal row 264 — presumes exactly this), so the floor on its far side begins 24 px later than a 48-px lattice would put it: **tile parity flips across every shared wall**. Each room therefore carries its own `origin_px` on the 24-px grid and its tiles are counted in 48-px units from that origin. This is a storage-unit refinement of "tiles on the 48-px grid", not a new tile size: `TILE_PX` stays 48, `V` is unchanged, and the alternatives are rejected — a double wall between rooms (a 48-px-thick shared wall needs two door frames in line and two Graph openings per passage, or a 48-deep frame the art bible does not define) and a full-48 wall row with a 24-px walkable skirt owned by no tile. The **sill** — the door-width × 24-px floor strip inside a doorway — is not a tile and does not count in `V`: each door declares a `sill_room` (one of its two flanking rooms) and `room_at(section_id, px)` answers `sill_room` for a px on the sill, so there is no walkable point in a section where `room_at` answers `NONE`.

**LY-6 — Identity, allocation and the migration stance.**
(a) *Ids.* Layout allocates `section_id` from `next_section_id`, `body_id` from `next_body_id` and `room_id` (a u32) from `next_room_id` **in template room order at `build_section`**, contiguous per instance (`room_id = room_id_base + room_index`). Ids are never reused and never renumbered (the Graph's append-only pattern, LS-15). A discarded section keeps its row as a tombstone (LY-19), so its ids stay consumed.
(b) *Keys.* Template-local keys (`room_key`, `socket_key`, `hp_key`, `door_key`, `node_ref`, `edge_ref`) are strings used for lint, diagnostics, migration and restore verification. The block persists only numeric ids, socket ordinals and the `template_id` string.
(c) *Graph ids.* The Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids from its own `next_*` counters in template order (LSG:170, LSG:180). Layout persists, per instance, `graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` so a template-local `node_ref` / `edge_ref` index maps to a numeric Graph id by `base + index` and a compartment id maps to its room by `comp_base`, deterministically. The seam id in `welds[]` is the Graph's `seam_id` (LSG:72 SeamRecord); Layout allocates no seam id.
(d) **ANSWERED by the Graph (LS-15, LS-19, M1 row; *Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass*); the ask is closed (OQ-4).** M1 `instantiate_section(section_id, template_id, kind)` takes a caller section id and now returns `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`, which Layout stores as `graph_ref_base`; M1 advances the Graph's persisted `next_section_id` to `max(section_id) + 1`, so Layout allocates the section id and the Graph's counter follows it. `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}` and `seam_view(seam_id)` is a pure read of `{state, sub_edges[], leak_bp, opening_ids[]}`; Layout uses `opening_ids[]` for the mated-hatch leaf map (LY-11, LY-16). The only mismatch case left is the restore-time guard of Edge Cases ("Save, restore and drift"). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
(e) *Migration stance, stated here and again in Open Questions:* "A renamed `room_key` or `template_id` needs a migration step in the owner once the first build has been given outside the project (SL-14, SL:219); before that, saves are disposable (SL-14)." This closes Save/Load Open Question 12 (SL:1300) and the Graph's Open Question 9 (LSG:1158) from the Layout side. Because the persisted ids are numeric and assigned at build, a template that merely *reorders* rooms changes ids only for NEW instances; existing saves keep theirs.

#### 1.2 Rectangles, walls, frames

**LY-7 — The footprint rectangle record and flags** (registry: `layout_rect_flags`)**.** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, stored as packed integer arrays plus one flags byte, **half-open** `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` over pixel CELLS (the tile grid, the foot box and sprite rows are all cells). Flags: `SOLID` (blocks `LocomotionStep`), `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` (the Emitter's `occludes_light`, EM-20), `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL`. Rects are SIMULATION DATA (kernel H10): never read back from the scene tree, never produced by an engine physics shape, and the avatar has no physics body. Layout never calls its own rects "collision shapes" (wording refresh routed in Cross-References). The only legal flag combinations (anything else is the lint error `RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`):

| Class | SOLID | OCCLUDES_LIGHT | DOOR_LEAF | PROP | MACHINE | HULL | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wall run | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/1 | HULL on exterior-facing runs |
| Door jamb | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | fixed, either side of the gap |
| Door leaf | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | always solid and occluding (no glass in MVP, EM-20); dynamic (LY-9) |
| Socket hatch plate (variant slot PLATE) while `FREE`, `CAPPED`, `CUT_OPEN` or `WELDED` one-sided | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | the plate covers the whole socket span (`width_tiles × 48` × 24); a reserved variant slot, not a static rect (LY-15). While `CUT_OPEN` it is solid AND occluding: nothing lies beyond a cut, and no avatar can leave the hull through it. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Socket jamb (variant slot JAMB), `WELDED` two-sided, `width_tiles >= 3` only | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | the hull bulkhead beside the 96-px hatch doorway, `(width_tiles × 48 − 96)` × 24; exterior hull wall, hence HULL; zero-width (omitted) at `width_tiles` 2. Same precedent as the hull-port row below: the HULL run compiles in parts with no SOLID overlap. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Tall prop / machinery node | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0/1 | 0 | `occludes_light` authored |
| Low prop | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | blocks feet, not light |
| Hull port (`wall_port` piece in a HULL run; routed from Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-19 / OQ-V2) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | blocks feet, passes light, so a residual lamp's light truthfully leaves the hull; its footprint replaces the HULL run's own over its span (the run compiles in two parts, no SOLID overlap) and `CONTAINMENT_LEAK` is unaffected because it is SOLID; it is absent from `rects_in`, not a translucent occluder, so EM-20 (f) is untouched |

275	**LY-16 — Recording a weld.** `attach_section(socket_a, socket_b, seam_id, welded_at_T)` (LM2, Class A) runs after the Graph's `weld_join` inside Assembly's single `apply` (KRN:197: single commands "whose `apply` calls published mutators on Graph, Layout and Body"). It appends a `welds[]` row `{seam_id, section_a, socket_a, section_b, socket_b, welded_at_T, state ACTIVE}`; sets both sockets `WELDED(seam_id)`; re-bases every section of the absorbed body by D.6 and moves them onto the host body; marks the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switches the variant slots of both sockets (LY-15), **initialises each newly active LEAF closed (`leaf_w = width_px`, consistent with `weld_join`'s new opening starting at `area` 0, Assembly MSA-15) and seeds the last-projected `leaf_w` cache with that value in the same `apply`, so the hatch span is solid from the instant the PLATE switches off; `layout.doors` re-derives `leaf_w` from the opening's `area` in P3 and changes nothing while `area` is still 0** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: BLOCKING, the LEAF slot had no initial state at weld time, so a P2 reader between the weld and the P3 hook saw an open gap)*, rebuilds the grid; bumps `version` (and `static_version`, LY-12 d) of **every section whose socket state changed — the host section of `socket_a`/`socket_b` whether or not it moves — and of every moved section**, and marks the dirty keys of LY-32: `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>`, and `SEC/<id>` for each of those sections. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text bumped moved sections only, so the unmoved host's PLATE → JAMB + LEAF change was invisible to a version-keyed consumer.)* The bump reports REGION for the two socket-host sections and FRAME for the other moved sections (LY-12 d); `body_of` of every moved section changes in this apply (absorbed -> survivor) and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick; Emitter State derives its `body_id` from it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The mated hatch's opening ids are read from the Graph (`seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`, ordinal = the index in `socket_plan.openings[]`) into a derived cache `opening_leaves` (edge id → the leaf slots it drives, LY-11); the cache is not persisted and is rebuilt in `post_restore` (LY-26 d). **Host rule (deterministic, argument-order independent):** the surviving body is the body with the **lower `body_id`** (the older body; the home-ship, built first, in the MVP). `socket_a` and `socket_b` are re-labelled internally by survivor, not by argument order, so D.6's `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a − pos_b` always places the *absorbed* frame in the *survivor's* frame and `frame_shift_px` has one sign convention; a call with reversed arguments therefore produces the identical result, and the dissolved body is never the home-ship's by an argument mix-up. `welds[]` is **canonicalised**: it records the survivor-side section and socket as `section_a`/`socket_a` and the absorbed side as `section_b`/`socket_b` whatever the call order, so a reversed call produces a byte-identical block and `layout_hash`. Layout returns `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}` (`frame_shift_px` as defined in D.6: the absorbed frame origin in the host frame, added to every moved section's offset) so Body can emit `BODY_TRANSFER` (PIPE:694) and keep the avatar's screen position where the layout allows — Body's concern. A weld **moves nothing already built** (the Graph's LS-15): only the absorbed body's frame is re-based, a translation of whole tiles. Layout records no `q` (Assembly's) and no cut mode until a cut (LY-17).
276	
277	**LY-17 — Recording a cut; detach and body ids.** `detach_section(seam_id, boundary_mode)` (LM3, Class A) runs after the Graph's `cut_detach` (LSG:172). It marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` (SEALED) or `CUT_OPEN` (RAGGED); then runs connected components over the ACTIVE `welds[]` in ascending `section_id`. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other component receives a NEW `body_id` from `next_body_id` (KRN:197: "Detach allocates a new body ID from the Layout block") and its `origin_section_id` is **`m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component** (D.12 — the same section whose origin becomes the new frame origin); its offsets are re-based so its frame origin is its minimum-id section's origin (D.12). **Dirty keys and versions (the rule of LY-12 d):** `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>`, and `SEC/<id>` plus a `version` and `static_version` bump for **every section whose socket state changed (both sections of the seam, the kept-side section even though it does not move) and every moved section**. If the hatch was open when it was cut (`area` > 0), the kept section's LEAF slot goes inactive and its PLATE goes active in the same apply, so the bump is what tells a version-keyed consumer that a light gap has become a solid plate. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The bump reports REGION for the two socket-host sections and FRAME for the other moved sections (LY-12 d); `body_of` of every moved section changes in this apply (kept/new split) and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick; Emitter State derives its `body_id` from it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **Entombment: who owns the guarantee that no actor stands where the PLATE materialises** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the severity is RECOMMENDED because the crisis cut and lethal friendly fire make the state reachable and AC-28 treats such an overlap as a Body defect)*: **Layout performs no actor check** (it reads nothing from `body.state`, LY-18) and `apply` places the PLATE unconditionally. On the **CHANNEL cut path** the guarantee is Assembly's: the completion `validate` blocks the cut outright (`MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`, MSA-21) while any crewmate's foot box overlaps the open hatch passage, using `detach_preview`'s `rects[]` (the PLATE footprint) as the test region. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* There is no cut path around Assembly's completion `validate`: CHANNEL rejects with `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED` and CASCADE (the "crisis" cut) defers and is abandoned on expiry, never forced (MSA-21, MSA-22). As a net behind that, Body REFUSES (it does not eject; BDY-24 iii, ruled 2026-10-28, delegated ruling G6): `rebase_on_detach` takes this record's `rects[]` and returns `-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP`, writing nothing, if a foot box overlaps them. Layout still performs no actor check. `detach_section` also checks `CAPACITY` in its validate (LY-29). Returns `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}`, where `rects[]` is exactly `detach_preview(seam_id).rects[]` (the seam's hatch rectangles, one per side, pre-cut body frame, computed before the sockets change) so prediction and apply cannot drift *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **A cut through a compartment is not representable:** a cut is requested only by `seam_id` (LSG:849 "Cuts happen only along seams, never through a compartment"), so Layout has no "cut here" geometry input. A cut never splits gas by a volume ratio because a compartment belongs to one section (LSG:172).
278	
279	**LY-18 — Bodies, membership and the Body boundary.** Layout owns `bodies[]`, each `section_instances[].body_id`, offsets, and `welds[]`. Ship Body owns pose, velocity, actor positions, kinematics and any engine-side shapes built from Layout data. Body repeats *(Ship Body & Interior Physics is designed; BDY repeats this)*: its ownership of `body.state` (pose, velocity, actor positions); `restore_after: [layout.state]`; and the physics PROJECTOR (KRN:197, KRN:198). Layout reads nothing from `body.state` (acyclic). *Correction surfaced to the 2D Lighting stage:* its brief says "Ship Body owns frames and `body_id`"; the kernel's "Detach allocates a new body ID from the Layout block" (KRN:197) decides it — Layout allocates the id and owns membership; Body owns the frame's POSE. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
280	
281	**LY-19 — Discard.** `discard_section_geometry(section_id)` (LM4, Class A) runs after the Graph's `discard_section` M4, which requires no ACTIVE seam (LSG:172). Precondition: no `WELDED` socket, else `SECTION_WELDED`. It marks the instance row `discarded` (a **tombstone**: ids are retained so they are never reused — the Graph's LS-21 form), removes its rects from the grid, dissolves its sole body and bumps `version`. Weld-history rows that name the section stay (Pillar 5), and the surviving mate's socket keeps its `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN` state. Items that lay in the section belong to Interaction and are carried or destroyed by the orchestrating apply (CR-9 atomicity), not by Layout.
282	
283	#### 1.4 Slots, anchors, derived promises
284	
285	**LY-20 — Hardpoints are Layout declarations; the Item DB decides what fits.** HARDPOINT fields per LY-4. The Graph's ABSENT or installed node is the runtime state; `compatible_defs(h)` (IDB F-6, IDB:577-594) is the Item DB's pure function, called by Layout's STRUCTURAL lint: every hardpoint has at least one compatible def; a LOAD (kind 13) hardpoint without `accepted_subtypes` is a lint ERROR (heater and lamp share a port signature) — this unblocks IDB AC-18 (IDB:1180). `socket_tag` is an advisory lint hint, never authoritative; port types are (IDB:169). A hardpoint's footprint rect (`MACHINE` flag, static) stays whether or not a module is installed: a pedestal or mount remains after salvage and Layout has no dependency on node state. The nouns stay distinct: **HARDPOINT** (module slot, node-backed) versus **LOOSE SLOT** (LY-22); the index's "salvage/module slots" means both.
286	
287	**LY-21 — A HULL_SEGMENT has no hardpoint.** The hull plate is a PART, not a module (HULL_SEGMENT has no `def_id`, IDB-5, LSG:185). `plate_positions[]` per HULL_SEGMENT = the host wall-face tile set (the Graph's `tiles` field, LSG:68), `bound_room_key`, and `exposed` (true iff the run is HULL); `segment_at(face_tile) -> segment_key | NONE` is a read, and `plate_positions(section_id)` lists the records in ascending HULL_SEGMENT node id (template order). It is the input of Adaptive Audio's `hull_anchor` derivation (AA-17, registry `hull_anchor`: the floor-division centroid of the lowest-id HULL_SEGMENT's plate set composed with `section_offset`), which Layout confirms as the contract (CX-A4); Layout publishes no `hull_anchor` read, because Layout's geometry reads answer section-local by default (LY-3 c). The DESTROYED-segment replacement path (LSG:755 against M5's ABSENT/SALVAGED precondition, IDB Open Questions 1 and 11) stays routed to the Graph and Item DB owners (C-9); Layout states only the geometry. Precondition for the MVP slice's seven HULL_SEGMENTs (LSG:228): every room tagged `outer` has at least `HULL_RUNS_MIN` disjoint exterior wall runs **that bear a FACE (a `CAP_ONLY` run, including every HULL run on a room's south edge, D.14, has no face to carry a plate and is not counted)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, each long enough for a segment's face tiles, separated by `SEGMENT_GAP_MIN_PX` so two breach trails do not overlap at the wall base; plate positions of different segments never share a wall tile (lints `OUTER_ROOM_HULL_RUNS`, `SEGMENT_TILE_SHARED`).
288	
289	**LY-22 — Loose slots and story slots; no item table.** LOOSE SLOT = `{slot_id, room_key, anchor_px, surface FLOOR|SHELF|CRATE, allowed_class[], capacity 1}`. The authored start placement `{def_id, count, condition_bp}` is Derelict Authoring's CONTENT, expanded to an ItemInstance by the Item DB's `fresh_instance` and placed by Interaction's `place_loose(inst, section_id, pos_px)` at world build *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Layout's schema reserves NO item table**: the loose-item holder is Interaction's `interaction.state` *(orchestrator ruling; Interaction is designed and IA-36 adds it)*, which adds `layout.state` to its own `restore_after`. One writer per fact (kernel H3): Interaction performs every instance move (IDB:426-452), and atomicity with a discard or detach is given by CR-9 whichever owner's mutator holds the rows. Layout supplies `loose_slots(section_id)`, `floor_tile_at(section_id, px) -> tile | NONE` (placement validity) and `body_of(section_id)`; an item position is `(section_id, pos_px section-local)`, so a weld or a detach moves nothing. STORY SLOT (Vertical Slice; art bible 6.5 ("one cause, one verb, one absence per wreck", placed as three tagged slots)) = `{slot_id, role CAUSE|VERB|ABSENCE, room_key, anchor_px}`; the list is reserved in schema v1, empty and lint-checked in MVP, so the Vertical Slice addition is not a `schema_version` bump. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
290	
291	**LY-23 — Anchors.** `anchor_geometry(anchor) -> {kind WALL_FACE|FLOOR, host_face_id, base_px_polyline[], sort_origin_y, section_id}` (FT:306 names verbatim). The Graph descriptor anchor `(node_id, port_local_index)` or `edge_id` (LSG:152-153, "Layout supplies the polyline") maps to a template anchor through `section_of(id)` and `graph_ref_base` (id minus base = template-local index). The polyline is axis-aligned, integer, wall part first then floor part (FT-13); `edge_len_px = Σ|Δ|` (D.8) and must not exceed `TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` (1152, 24 tiles — the Failure & Trail knob's content bound, owned here as a lint: Layout REJECTS a longer polyline and never shortens it, FT:642). It returns nothing, without error, for an id whose section is DISCARDED (FT:703-704: the draw must not crash). `sort_origin_y` is per Pipeline D.12 for WALL_FACE and `NONE` for pure FLOOR anchors (floor marks are not Y-sorted). `subject_anchors(section_id) -> [{local_key, kind_hint DOOR_FACE|HARDPOINT|SOCKET|SLOT|CONSOLE|INSTRUMENT, anchor_px, room_id, console_role}]` where `console_role` is `POD` or `DOCK` and is present iff `kind_hint` is `CONSOLE` (a structural lint `CONSOLE_ROLE_UNSET`, ERROR, rejects a CONSOLE anchor without a role and a role on any other kind); Layout asserts no placement: Derelict Authoring authors them (a POD anchor in every dock room, a DOCK anchor in the home airlock only; its lints `POD_CONSOLE_MISSING` and `DOCK_CONSOLE_MISSING`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: two DOOR_FACE anchors per **interior** door, one per face, each `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` outside the leaf's occupied span (EM:208 e); **a socket hatch gets ONE inner-face DOOR_FACE per hatch per section, plus its WELD_SOCKET anchor** (the outer face lies in void or in the mate's wall, which would conflict with `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE` and `DOOR_APPROACH_CLEAR`, so no outer-face anchor is placed; the mate's own section carries its own inner-face anchor) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; "Layout places, Interaction names the kind and registers". Presentation rebuilds anchors statelessly from Layout on Layout's `SEC/<id>` and the Graph's `T`/`SEC/<id>` (FT:265, FT AC-107). A wall fitting with no floor-run record is a lint error (`WALL_FITTING_NO_RUN`, FT:703), not a hidden trail. Layout must not grow a "trail" field: Failure & Trail reads Graph descriptors only and has no block (FT:26).
292	
293	**LY-24 — `V` and `exposed_tiles` never change while a room exists.** The MVP promise to the Graph, as rule text: "`V` and `exposed_tiles` of an instantiated room never change while the room exists" (LSG:840 is the Vertical Slice re-base rule, not an MVP path). `V` is D.3. `exposed_tiles(room)` is the sum of the lengths of the room's HULL wall-run segments (D.4), static at build; socket frames and plate positions lie inside HULL runs (lint) so they are counted once, and a weld does not change it. The **conservative error** this accepts: a welded, closed hatch still radiates as hull. It is quantified in Edge Cases (the single MVP socket is 2 of the fixture airlock's 6 exposed tiles, D.4; a larger outer room would carry 20-40) and the Vertical Slice re-base is routed to the Graph owner in Open Questions. The Graph's lint ranges (`V` 4-200, `exposed_tiles` 0-80, LSG:299, LSG:452) are the Graph's variable ranges (not reason codes); Layout's structural lint reports a room outside them under its own lint ids `V_RANGE` and `EXPOSED_RANGE` and restates no bound. *Which value governs (answers Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-13):* D.4 evaluated on the loaded template's HULL runs governs everywhere, including across a 24-px jog (each run's `len_tiles` counts once); an authoring design table is documentation, and Authoring's `EXPOSED_DRIFT` WARN (tolerance 1 tile) reports where the two differ.
294	
295	#### 1.5 Construction, restore, mutators, reads
296	
297	**LY-25 — World construction order.** `build_section(template_id, kind) -> {section_id, body_id}` (LM1, Class A) = allocate ids → record the instance on its own NEW body at `offset_px` (0, 0) (the body frame's origin is its minimum-id section's origin, D.12) → Graph M1 `instantiate_section(section_id, template_id, kind)` (the Graph's own table names the caller "Layout / derelict build, home-ship setup", LSG:180; `kind` is an argument forwarded to M1 and is **not persisted by Layout** — the Graph's section record owns it, LS-17, LSG:174) → store `graph_ref_base` → build the grid → bump `version`. **Every built section starts on its own body, and every multi-section body is produced by welds only** (authored welds in Vertical Slice procgen use `attach_section` with `welded_at_T` 0): there is no "place on an existing body" path, so the weld relation stays a forest (LY-14) and the component split of LY-17 stays exact. **Layout calls NO Emitter or Interaction mutator.** The orchestrating atomic apply — Web Map & Transit's `init_world(world_seed)` per Save/Load SL-18 (SL:255, run in `LOADING` in `restore_after` order under a WriteScope), the only caller of LM1 (the pod is built there once, as one persistent body, and a pod hop builds nothing — Web Map CF-LY; Assembly never discards (MSA-24) and is not an LM1 caller (C11)) — calls, inside one WriteScope and in this fixed order: Layout `build_section` → Emitter E1 `instantiate_section_emitters(section_id)` (its stated caller stays "Assembly / Web Map atomic apply", EM:147) → Interaction `sync_section(section_id)` → PROJECTOR notification *(Web Map & Transit and Interaction are designed; the call order is theirs to repeat)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Layout supplies their data through reads (`subject_anchors`, `loose_slots`, LY-22, LY-23). This keeps `restore_after: []` honest: Layout depends on nothing at restore. The MVP world (home-ship + derelict A + derelict B + the always-dormant pod: four sections on four bodies, registry `mvp_template_roster`) is a data file `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` consumed by `init_world`; the floor plans in it are Derelict Authoring's. The build is incremental and the PROJECTOR reports ready when its scene content exists; Transit's `ARRIVING` is the fixed-length state `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` 45 ticks; the Pipeline, not the sim, holds the black plate for any PROJECTOR lag (a large section may exceed one tick — `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is a logging threshold, not a cut-off).
298	
299	**LY-26 — Restore, the two validity classes, and template drift.**
300	(a) `restore(data, stored_version)` replaces the instance tables whole into scratch and swaps only on success; an unsupported `stored_version` is a reported failure, never a silent default. The snapshot obeys SL-2 (SL:176): no `Vector2i`, `Rect2`, `Color` or `Resource`; integer vectors travel as two ints or a packed integer array; dictionary keys are String or int; 64-bit values (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`) never travel as JSON numbers. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Concrete encoding rules** (JSON text turns int keys into strings and numbers into floats; the payload itself is `var_to_bytes` binary, SL-2, but the dev `dump-save` JSON and the generic K-3 round-trip test must not change a table's meaning): (1) **no integer-keyed Dictionary** — every table (instances, sockets, welds, bodies) is a dense set of parallel packed arrays in ascending id order, so a stringified key can never be misread; the few Dictionaries are String-keyed and hold only scalars and packed arrays; (2) **64-bit values** (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`; and `layout_hash` wherever Save/Load's header carries it, which is not `layout.state`, D.10 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) travel as **two 32-bit int halves** `(hi, lo)`, each normalised with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` before any compare (D.10) — the project convention (Interaction `last_salvage_T`, Assembly `last_shape_change_T`, and D.21's two-int count) — and are rendered as exact-width lowercase hex strings only by Save/Load's header and the dev dump (SL-2 S-1), never as a JSON number; (3) **`snapshot()` deep-copies**: it returns fresh packed arrays, never a reference into the live block, so a mutation after `snapshot()` cannot reach a captured snapshot (and a captured snapshot cannot be mutated into the live block).
301	(b) *Class 1 — static queries, valid immediately after `restore()` returns.* Every query that depends only on templates and the instance table — `room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `room_surface`, `socket_plan`, `anchor_geometry`, static `rects_in`, `section_offset`, `body_of` — is valid at once, because templates were loaded in BOOTING and the instance table is the only restored state. This makes the Graph's loud failure (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM` on mis-order, LSG:831) impossible by construction whatever the order of `post_restore` calls.
302	(c) *Class 2 — leaf-dependent results, valid only after Layout's own `post_restore()`.* DOOR_LEAF rects depend on the Graph's persisted `area`, which Layout cannot read inside its own `restore()` (the Graph restores after Layout) and which the Graph now publishes as `opening(edge_id) -> {area, area_max, door_state}` (LY-10; the ask is closed, OQ-3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **(orchestrator ruling; routed amendment to the Layout-side promise "every query is valid immediately after restore":)** leaves are derived by one `derive_doors` pass in Layout's `post_restore` (the kernel guarantees every `restore()` has completed before any `post_restore()` begins, KRN:843, so the Graph's persisted `area` is in memory whatever the order of the `post_restore` calls) and thereafter by `layout.doors`. Between `restore()` and `post_restore()` leaf-dependent queries (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage` (reports `open_extent_px` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) report the TEMPLATE default (every leaf closed) and raise a `stale_leaf` diagnostic flag if read. **Self-heal:** Layout's `post_restore` bumps `version(section_id)` (1 → 2) for every section whose derived leaf set differs from the all-closed template default; LY-12(d)'s "a restore is an unconditional rebuild signal" and the Emitter's W0 `version` read (EM:227) therefore rebuild the Emitter's static layer on tick 1 with no ordering between the two `post_restore` calls, and `body.integrate after: layout.doors` (LY-10) covers every P3 reader. Whether `post_restore` order follows `restore_after` is **informational only** (CR-8 and KRN:843 say "after every `restore()`"); no Layout rule depends on the answer. The `stale_leaf` diagnostic and this restore path are **live behaviour**, not a stand-in for an unanswered ask: they stay as specified now that the Graph read exists, because the window between `restore()` and `post_restore()` is real whatever the Graph publishes. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `post_restore` also bumps `leaf_version` (never `static_version`) for each such section, and rebuilds the derived `opening_leaves` map from the restored `welds[]` and `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`.
303	(d) `post_restore()` does cross-block VERIFICATION only: every `graph_ref_base` resolves (node, edge and compartment counts match the template), every installed `def_id` at a hardpoint resolves in the Item DB catalogue (a diagnostic, not a hard fail), and every `welds[]` `seam_id` resolves to a Graph SeamRecord. Failures use the restore reason set (LY-29).
304	(e) *Template drift.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The single `template_hash` is **split in two**, both persisted per instance (D.10): `geometry_hash` (u32; the canonical bytes of everything that decides where a rect, tile, socket, door or anchor is — room `origin_px` and tile runs, wall runs and the compiled rect table, socket `facing`/`line_px`/`start_px`/`width_tiles`/`hatch`, door positions and `area_max`, hardpoint cells, anchor polylines) and `visual_hash` (u32; kit-piece ids, art references, dialect, labels, hinted flags that no query reads). `restore` refuses an unknown `template_id` (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE`) and a STRUCTURAL change (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`: the sets of `room_key`, `socket_key`, `hp_key`, `node_ref`, or any room's tile set differ) **and a geometry change on an instance that carries history** — `geometry_hash` differs and the instance has any non-`FREE` socket, any `welds[]` row naming it, or shares its body with another section — because a moved socket, wall edge or doorway under a welded or cut instance restores with broken abutment while every key set still matches (a socket position or wall rect edit used to classify as "visual-only"). A geometry change on a never-welded `FREE` instance alone is accepted with one diagnostic `geometry_changed_fresh` (nothing depends on it yet and its rects are re-derived from the new template); a `visual_hash` difference alone is accepted with one diagnostic. Pre-release saves are disposable (SL-14, adopted verbatim); after the first build given outside the project the migration obligation of LY-6(e) applies. `rot_q` must be 0 (LY-3 d).
305	
306	**LY-27 — Mutators.** Layout has four mutators, all Class A (command-backed, validate-then-apply, CR-9) and **no Class B** (clamp-never-reject): it holds no quantity that can sensibly be clamped. Each has a pure `can_*` validate query; `apply` is infallible once validated (a failure inside `apply` is a defect and sends the kernel to `FAULTED`).
