**LY-9 — The door leaf is ONE sliding rectangle derived from the Graph's `area`.** For a door or a mated hatch with doorway width `width_px` (96 in every dialect — the 96×96 door cell, art bible 8.2) and the Graph opening's `area` and the template's `area_max`: `leaf_w = width_px − floor(width_px × area / area_max)` (D.5). The leaf is a rect of depth `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 along the doorway, `leaf_w` long, anchored to the **hinge side**; it retracts into the wall pocket on that side (for an interior door the pocket is part of the adjacent wall run, so no extra rect; for a socket hatch the pocket is presentation only and exempt from `DOOR_POCKET_CLEAR`, LY-15 e *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). `area = 0` → `leaf_w = width_px` (the leaf covers the doorway); `area = area_max` → `leaf_w = 0` (no rect is returned). Flags `SOLID | OCCLUDES_LIGHT | DOOR_LEAF`. The same rect is the collision input (PCI:103), the occluder rect (EM-20 d) and the drawn leaf's extent (the PROJECTOR sizes the sprite from it), so **collision and light cannot disagree** (Pillar 1). In the MVP the Graph's `area` jumps 0 ↔ `area_max` in one tick (IA-24), so the leaf is binary by consequence and no text may promise a sliding leaf (LY-11, Option A); the formula has no threshold, so `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` (EM:788-789, "only if the leaf is binary") is **RETIRED by this GDD** — a registry supersede (`status: deprecated`, superseded-by D.5), never a silent delete (R23 handling in Cross-References). The gap a body passes through is `width_px − leaf_w = floor(width_px × area / area_max)`; a foot box passes iff the gap is at least the box's extent across the doorway — Body supplies the box as an argument (LY-11), and for the MVP foot box of 16×8 (PCI:103) that is 16 px across a doorway in an E-W wall and 8 px across one in a N-S wall (D.5, `area_pass_min`).
*Hinge rule for mated hatches (CLARIFY, adopted).* Two Layout leaves (one per section) project one mated hatch's single `area` (LY-15). If their pockets lay on different sides the one `area` would produce two different gaps and one leaf would cover the other's opening — two truths from one value, a Pillar 1 break. A socket hatch's pocket side is therefore **fixed by the socket's axis, not authored**: the LOW-coordinate side (north for E/W-facing sockets, west for N/S-facing sockets); a hatch that declares a hinge is the lint error `HATCH_HINGE_AUTHORED`. The rule is **sound only because welds are pure translation (LY-3 d)**: both sections then share one axis orientation, so "LOW side" is the same side in both frames. Interior doors keep an authored `hinge LOW|HIGH`.
*Unit note (C-6, not resolved here).* The Graph states `area` in 1/64 tile with `A_HOLE_MAX` 64 "one door's worth" (LSG:72, LSG:323), while a door is two tiles wide. D.5 is unit-free (a ratio `area / area_max`); each door and hatch template declares its own `area_max`, a lint checks it against the door width, and the Graph owner is asked to state what 1/64 tile means for a door two tiles wide. **ASK (Graph owner).**

**LY-10 — `layout.doors`: Layout's only hook, and the P2/P3 correctness condition.** Registration (CR-3): `hook_id layout.doors`, owner Layout, divisor 1, offset 0, `after: []`. It runs in P3 and, for every loaded door and hatch, re-derives the leaf rect from the opening's `area` — read through the Graph's published `opening(edge_id) -> {area, area_max, door_state}` (LS-19 additions, *Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass*; the ask this GDD made is **answered and closed**, OQ-3) — updates the dynamic leaf list and bumps `leaf_version(section_id)` (and so `version`, LY-12 d; never `static_version`) once per section whose leaf set changed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (changed = any `leaf_w` differs from the last projected value; the last-projected cache is derived, not persisted). Cost: a loop over at most `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` doors, an integer multiply and divide each (≈ 20 in MVP). **Correctness condition, stated as a rule and tested: the `area` and `door_state` of every OPENING Layout PROJECTS — template doors and mated hatches — change only in P2** — M13 `set_opening_area` is a command-backed Class A mutator (LSG:192) and commands apply in P2 (CR-2) — so a P3 hook sees same-tick state (the mirror of Controller PC-18 test 7: a closed leaf blocks and an open one does not in the SAME tick its state changes). **Virtual openings have no leaf:** the Graph derives breach holes and seam weeps as VIRTUAL OPENINGs on every run of its failure hook in P3 (LS-5, LSG:72), so "area changes only in P2" is false for them, and Layout neither projects nor reads them (their gas effect is the Graph's; their trail is Failure & Trail's). Stated consequences: (i) the `CLOSING_BLOCKED` retry (PCI:650, "retries on each of its hook runs") must be a SYSTEM-origin command processed at T+1 (CR-9 b), never M13 called from a P3 hook — adopted by Interaction (IA-24, registry `door_attempt`); (ii) **confirmed by the Graph owner (scoped identically; the Graph's Interactions row for Layout states "no Graph phase writes `area` or `door_state`", *Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass*)** that no Graph phase writes `area` or `door_state` of a template door or a mated hatch; (iii) **resolved (Ship Body BDY-8, registry `body_state_block`):** `body.integrate` is registered `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]` (Controller PC-14 and PC-15 read the same) — because a registration-order tie-break would work by accident and CR-3 forbids relying on it.
**RESOLVED (Ship Body BDY-8, registry `body_state_block`):** `body.integrate` is registered by its owner, Ship Body, as `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`, and Controller PC-14 / PC-15 read the same. The Emitter needs no edit for correctness: EM-1 registers `emitter.place` as `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]` (EM:104, EM:321), and CR-3 resolves a topological order over `after` transitively, so once `body.integrate` is `after: layout.doors`, `emitter.place` is ordered after `layout.doors` already. An explicit `layout.doors` entry in EM-1's list is **optional, explicit** (EM-23 at EM:227 may add it for readability).

**RESOLVED (Interaction IA-24, registry `door_attempt`): the attempt completion and the `CLOSING_BLOCKED` retry are SYSTEM-origin commands applied in P2 of T+1 with `leaf_would_overlap` called from validate (LY-10 i adopted); no M13 call from a P3 hook.** `interaction.step` never calls M13 (IA-24 c/d, IA D.12): at `T == Tb + DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` it submits a SYSTEM `set_opening {target_ref, area}` command, and a door in `CLOSING_BLOCKED` has its command re-submitted each tick by Interaction's `attempts[]`, so every `area` write of a template door or mated hatch lands in P2 and the same-tick guarantee of this rule holds (`layout.doors after: [interaction.step]` would be a cycle and is not needed). OQ-14 (a) is closed. *Historical fallback, no longer needed (the amendment landed via Ship Body BDY-8; recorded in Open Questions OQ-6):* lazy derive on read, stamped by the Graph's write state rather than by tick, with no hook and no amendment — its defects are that a read mutates a derived cache and that a refresh in P2 can precede a later same-P2 change to `area`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**LY-11 — Door-close safety.** The invariant "a footprint rect may never be enabled while it overlaps an actor's foot box" (PCI:650) is Layout rule text, enforced as follows. Layout publishes the PURE query `leaf_would_overlap(opening_ref, area, foot_boxes[]) -> bool` (D.5), whose first argument is the **opening**, not one section's door *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a mated hatch is two leaf rects (one per section) driven by one `area` (LY-15), and a 16-px foot box straddling the seam can overlap only the far section's leaf, so a check validated against one section's `door_ref` would pass while the other leaf grows over the body (the PCI:650 invariant broken on the MVP's only hatch). Layout therefore evaluates **every leaf projected from that opening, on both sections, against every foot box, and returns true if any overlaps**. **Foot boxes are arguments, supplied by the caller from Body's read view as opaque half-open rectangles**; Layout never reads `body.state` (acyclic restore) and does not define the foot box — Body fixes it (BDY-14, registry `foot_box`: the foot origin is the box's TOP row, box `[pos.x − 8, pos.x + 8) × [pos.y, pos.y + 8)`), and Layout's guarantee stays stated on rectangles and caller boxes. The check runs for the NEW `area` of **every write that raises `leaf_w`** (a close): under the MVP's binary door model (below) that is the one jump to `area` 0 and each T+1 retry of `CLOSING_BLOCKED`; were a stepped slide ever introduced (Option B, OQ-14 c) it would run on every step, because the leaf grows each step. A body standing in the doorway therefore halts the closure at the first overlapping write and nothing is displaced. Layout returns the bool only; the reason code is the verb owner's, Interaction's: a PLAYER-origin close is rejected `OBSTRUCTED` (IA-24; PCI:650 left the code to Layout and Interaction to confirm, and its `BLOCKED` wording is a refresh routed to the Controller owner, Cross-References B). **Retry owner:** Interaction's `attempts[]` holds the `CLOSING_BLOCKED` retry for both origins (seat 0 for a SYSTEM-origin close). **Travel — the MVP door model is BINARY (Option A, decided in the design review).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Layout owns no door clock: D.5 is evaluated on whatever `area` the Graph holds each tick. IA-24 and the registry `door_attempt` fix the MVP behaviour: a `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` (30) attempt window in which the leaf does not move, then one M13 jump of `area` 0 ↔ `area_max`. The leaf is therefore closed in one tick and open in the next, and **no player-facing text promises a leaf that slides**. Layout adds no latency of its own (the leaf is projected in the same tick's P3, LY-10), so the leaf's travel time is exactly one tick and the cross-system invariant `TAP_REARM_TICKS` (12) `>=` that travel time (Interaction I-8) holds trivially. **The sprite equals the rect (binding on the PROJECTOR):** the drawn leaf is sized from the Layout leaf rect of the same tick and **no tween, ease or interpolation may give the leaf sprite an extent different from the rect** — a "slide" added later for polish would show a leaf where the rect, the foot and the lamp beam say there is none, a Pillar 1 break. Motion that does not change the leaf's extent (the motor whine and its sound during the attempt window, an emissive frame sprite with **no `Light2D`**, which AC-122 forbids; *amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was 'a light on the frame'*) is Adaptive Audio's and the PROJECTOR's to add freely. A stepped slide (Option B) is a Vertical Slice option only: it would name its owner (Graph: a motor rate on M13; or Interaction: stepped commands), bind that owner to the `TAP_REARM_TICKS` invariant above, and re-open the per-step close check (OQ-14 c); until then Layout states the invariant and owns no value in it. On SYSTEM origin Interaction enters `CLOSING_BLOCKED` and retries at T+1 (LY-10 i), `area` stays at its last non-overlapping value, and the body is never displaced. Opening (raising `area`) is never blocked by Layout. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The obstructed cue (rect-honest, geometric):** a blocked close and an unpowered door are otherwise both just a motor whine, which would break the Game Feel promise that the "why" is always a geometric fact. Layout therefore also publishes the pure read `leaf_obstruction(opening_ref, area, foot_boxes[]) -> {box_index, leaf_slot}` (the first overlapping box in caller order and the leaf it overlaps, or `NONE`), so the verb owner and the PROJECTOR can point the cue at the obstruction itself — a stalled leaf edge and the blocking body — which an unpowered door can never produce, because an unpowered door never reaches the overlap test (IA-24: it resolves `PRECONDITION(NO_POWER)` at the end of the window). The cue's form and the decision whether it may surface during `CLOSING_BLOCKED` without becoming a power oracle (IA-24's uniform attempt window exists to prevent one) are Interaction's and the art-director's (cross-GDD note, OQ-31); Layout supplies the geometry and asserts nothing about the cue. The debug assert that PCI:650 attributes to "a Layout projection" can run only where the rect and the foot box are both visible — Body's sweep (`PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP`); this GDD says so and routes a one-line wording note to the Controller owner. **`opening_ref` is the Graph OPENING `edge_id`** — the same `target_ref` that Interaction's `set_opening {target_ref, area}` carries (IA-24) — so one name serves an interior door and a mated hatch. Layout resolves it through a derived map `opening_leaves(edge_id) -> [(section_id, slot)]`: an interior door's opening is `edge_base + edge_ref index` (LY-6 c) and yields one leaf; a mated hatch's opening ids come from the weld (`seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`, LY-16) and yield **two** leaves, one per section, each at its own `section_offset`. The map is derived, never persisted, and rebuilt in `post_restore`. An `edge_id` that is not a projected opening returns false and raises the diagnostic `opening_unknown` (a validate-time defect of the caller, never a player-reachable state). Items are not actors: a loose item inside a door's footprint is not a foot box; **ASK (Interaction, designed; consistent with IA-28, which treats a cell as valid only where `floor_tile_at` returns a tile)**: door cells are `NO_LOOSE` (`floor_tile_at` returns `NONE` for them), a drop snaps to the nearest legal cell, and an authored item on a door cell is the lint error `LOOSE_ON_DOOR`. Interaction's earlier `foot_box_overlaps_leaf` is gone (IA-37); Layout uses only its own name `leaf_would_overlap`, which Interaction calls from `validate` (IA-24) *(Interaction is designed; its call site currently passes `door_ref = (section_id, door_index)` and reads `door_ref` in IA-24, its D.12 and the registry `door_attempt` variables — a refresh routed in Cross-References B so that it passes the opening's `target_ref`)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**LY-12 — The OccluderSource, the boundary convention, the broadphase and `version`.**
(a) *Seam.* `occluder_source(body_id) -> OccluderSource` exposes `rects_in(aabb)` and `version(section_id)` with EM-20's names verbatim (names unchanged; the out parameter of LY-12 e and the sibling `static_version` / `leaf_version` are additive). EM-20 names no `body_id` while EM-30 compares geometry only within one body, so each instance's `rects_in` answers in THAT body's frame, in ascending key `(section_id, idx)` (D.9) — the **reserved key set** is stable across a weld, a cut and a restore because an attach renumbers nothing: every piece that can ever exist at a socket (PLATE, JAMB, LEAF; LY-15) owns an `idx` from the template's compile, and a state change only switches slots between active and inactive (an inactive slot is omitted from results exactly like a `leaf_w` 0 rect). What changes on a weld is therefore the *active subset* of the sockets' slots, never a key. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
(b) *Boundary convention — stated once.* Integer coordinates in Layout name pixel CELLS. A stored rect `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` therefore *occupies* cells `x0..x1−1`, `y0..y1−1`. **One convention per function, no exceptions** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: every box a caller passes IN (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`'s foot boxes, D.2, D.9, D.22) is **half-open** `[ax0, ax1) × [ay0, ay1)`; every rect handed OUT by `rects_in` **and by `solid_in`** is the **occupied span** `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, so the Emitter's D.6 slab arithmetic is unchanged in code and Body's cell sweep reads the same numbers. (The earlier D.9 "closed query box" is retired; a half-open box of width `w` starting at `ax0` touches cells `floor_div(ax0, c)` to `floor_div(ax0 + w − 1, c)`.) Rule text: "the conservative closed test (EM-20 a, a graze blocks) is applied to the occupied span `[x0, x1−1] × [y0, y1−1]`; `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` is Chebyshev distance from that span" (D.2). A cell outside every occupied span — the first legal row south of a wall, Pipeline D.12 — is therefore not blocked at its origin, which is what EM-6's "outside every footprint by construction" (EM:157) assumes. The foot box's vertical placement is Body's; Layout's guarantee is stated on rectangles and on whatever box the caller passes: a box whose cells lie outside every occupied span is legal.
**CONFLICT C-1 (one-pixel example, not a rule change; routed to the Emitter owner):** EM:467 (D.6 example), EM:1013 (AC-22) and EM:1014 (AC-23) describe "wall x 408..432" as 25 closed points and reject an anchor at 432; under this rule the wall occupies 408..431, so (432, 200) passes with clearance 1 and (431, 200) fails; AC-22's three probes (540 blocked, 407 clear, 408 blocked) are unchanged. `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` is confirmed at 1 (range 1-2) and re-sourced to this GDD (Cross-References).
(c) *Broadphase.* A per-body uniform grid, cell `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` 48, derived, never persisted, rebuilt at build, attach, detach and restore (D.9). One structure serves Body's `solid_in`, the Emitter's segment test and Lighting; the Emitter's ADR candidate 4 ("the broadphase … and whether the spatial index lives in Layout or here", EM:32) is answered: **Layout**. `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` is sized to the Controller's performance criterion (PCI:1078: 2,000 rects, ≤ 0.05 ms per actor per tick at P99; spike, GDScript cost [UNV]). Callers issue ONE `solid_in` per actor per tick with the swept bounding box and sweep analytically against the result, never one query per 1-px step. Rejected: an Emitter-owned index (drift, double memory) and engine physics queries (EM-20: nondeterministic).
(d) *`version(section_id)`* is a monotone u32, NOT persisted, reset to 1 on `restore` (the Emitter rebuilds in its own `post_restore`; consumers must treat a restore as an unconditional rebuild signal, because a post-restore `version` can numerically equal a pre-restore cached value). It is bumped by `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section`, `discard_section_geometry`, `layout.doors` and Layout's own `post_restore` (LY-26 c, 1 → 2 for a section with an open leaf). MVP has no prop mutator (props are static); the bump list is closed so a Vertical Slice movable prop adds one entry deliberately. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Which sections are bumped (the rule, stated once):** every section whose rect set can change is bumped, *moved or not*. That is (i) every section whose **socket state changes** — both sections of the seam on a weld and on a cut, including the host section that does not move, because on a weld its PLATE becomes JAMB plus LEAF and on a cut its LEAF (possibly open, `area` > 0) becomes a solid PLATE, so a consumer keyed on `version` that missed the unmoved mate would keep passing light through a solid plate (a see-through-but-solid wall, the failure the secondary design test forbids); and (ii) every section whose body-frame offset changes (every moved section). Each such section also gets the dirty key `SEC/<id>`, and both bodies of the seam get `BODY/<id>` (LY-16, LY-17, LY-27). **Three counters, one contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `static_version(s)` is bumped by every cause above except a leaf change; `leaf_version(s)` is bumped only by `layout.doors` (and by `post_restore`'s self-heal for an open leaf); `version(s)` is the EM-20 name and is bumped whenever either is, so a consumer that rebuilds everything keys on `version` unchanged, while a consumer that can patch (the Emitter's static layer, the weld-preview memo) keys the static layer on `static_version` and the dynamic leaves on `leaf_version`. Animating a door therefore bumps `static_version` 0 times; a stepped slide (a Vertical Slice option, OQ-14 c) costs a leaf patch per tick, never a full static rebuild. All three are not persisted and reset to 1 on `restore`. **`changed_region(section_id)`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: a pure ordered read `changed_region(section_id) -> ALL | REGION(box) | FRAME`, valid for bumps applied in the current tick (cleared at the end of the tick; the Emitter reads it in W0 of the same tick, because `emitter.place` runs every tick after the P2 apply; NONE when no bump was applied to the section this tick); derived, never persisted (after a restore every section reports ALL once; `version` already resets to 1). Values: build, discard and `post_restore` = ALL (unchanged); a `layout.doors` leaf change = REGION(union box of the old and new leaf rectangles; Emitter ask E-N, unchanged); `attach_section` (LY-16) and `detach_section` (LY-17): for each of the two socket-host sections REGION(union box of that socket's PLATE, JAMB and LEAF slot rectangles, active and inactive, in the section's body frame); for every other moved section (the absorbed body's remaining sections, or the cut-off component's remaining sections) FRAME = a pure translation of the whole body (`rot_q` 0), geometry and slot sets unchanged. A socket-host section that also moves reports REGION; a reader detects its translation by comparing `section_offset(section_id)` with its cached value. The bumps of `version` and `static_version` are unchanged. The read tells the Emitter what kind of change a `static_version` bump was, so it can re-derive its `body_id` and keep its pair rows across a weld or cut without a full cold rebuild (Emitter S8 against S8b); a reader that does not read it treats every bump as ALL.
(e) *Allocation and the result contract.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The hot-path API is an **out-parameter** API: `rects_in(aabb, out: QueryBuffer)` and `solid_in(body_id, aabb, out: QueryBuffer)` fill a **caller-owned** `QueryBuffer` and return the record count; they return no array. A function that returned one shared reused buffer would alias between consumers (Body's sweep, the Emitter, Lighting and Interaction's throw all call within one tick) and cannot be both allocation-free and safe under copy-on-write, so each consumer owns one buffer and `clear()` resets its length without releasing capacity. **Record layout (structure of arrays, one index per record):** `keys: PackedInt64Array` — `rect_key = section_id × RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` reaches `2^32 − 1`, which overflows a 32-bit element for `section_id >= 2^19`, so the key column is 64-bit; `spans: PackedInt32Array` — four ints per record `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, the occupied span in the BODY frame (LY-12 b); `flags: PackedByteArray` — one LY-7 flags byte. Records are in ascending `rect_key`; a rect appears once per call (the broadphase de-duplicates a rect spanning several cells). A value-returning wrapper (`rects_in_copy`) may exist for tools and tests only and is not on a hot path. The steady-state call allocates nothing once each buffer has reached its working capacity. (→ ADR: packed-array buffer layout and the engine cost of `resize`, spike SP-ENG-1.)

#### 1.3 Sockets, seams, welds, bodies

**LY-13 — A socket is a pre-declared attachment site.** SOCKET = `{socket_key, facing N|E|S|W, line_px, start_px, width_tiles, class_id, lanes[] {loop, lane_index, node_ref, port_local_index}, hatch {door_key} | none}`. `line_px` is the OUTER face of the hull wall (the wall footprint lies inboard of it: for facing E the footprint is `[line_px − 24, line_px)`); `start_px` is the low end of the span along the run; `width_tiles` equals the seam length `L_seam` (1-12, LSG:328); the socket's reference point `pos_px` is `(line_px, start_px)` for E/W facings and `(start_px, line_px)` for N/S facings, in section-local px. A **lane** is one loop feed-through across the seam and is the Layout record that PRODUCES a Graph weld-plan pair `(node_a, port_a, node_b, port_b, loop)`; "pair" stays the Graph's noun and "lane" is Layout's (C-10). The number of authored sockets per section is at most `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION`, which is itself at most `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION` (8, LSG:916 — cited, not restated; content lint). **Socket states** (registry: `socket_state`)**:** `FREE → WELDED(seam_id)`, then `CAPPED` (after a SEALED cut) or `CUT_OPEN` (after a RAGGED cut, LSG:172). `CAPPED` and `CUT_OPEN` **never return to `FREE` in MVP**: the scar is history (Pillar 5), and no mutator exists that could do it (LY-27). MVP: exactly one socket on the home-ship (LSG:228) and its mate on derelict B.

*The four-facing table (stated once; the N/S rule used to appear only in a fixture)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `W` is `width_tiles`; the span along the run is `[start_px, start_px + W × 48)`; every footprint is 24 px deep; "LOW" is the coordinate-low end of the span, where the hatch is aligned and its leaf retracts (LY-9, LY-14, LY-15).

| Facing | Wall run orientation | Hull footprint (normal axis × span axis) | `pos_px` | LOW end of the span | Mate facing | PLATE rect | JAMB rect (`W` >= 3) | LEAF rect at `leaf_w` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E | N-S | `[line_px − 24, line_px) × [start_px, start_px + W·48)` | `(line_px, start_px)` | north (low y) | W | the whole footprint | `[line_px − 24, line_px) × [start_px + 96, start_px + W·48)` | `[line_px − 24, line_px) × [start_px, start_px + leaf_w)` |
| W | N-S | `[line_px, line_px + 24) × [start_px, start_px + W·48)` | `(line_px, start_px)` | north (low y) | E | the whole footprint | `[line_px, line_px + 24) × [start_px + 96, start_px + W·48)` | `[line_px, line_px + 24) × [start_px, start_px + leaf_w)` |
| S | E-W | `[start_px, start_px + W·48) × [line_px − 24, line_px)` | `(start_px, line_px)` | west (low x) | N | the whole footprint | `[start_px + 96, start_px + W·48) × [line_px − 24, line_px)` | `[start_px, start_px + leaf_w) × [line_px − 24, line_px)` |
| N | E-W | `[start_px, start_px + W·48) × [line_px, line_px + 24)` | `(start_px, line_px)` | west (low x) | S | the whole footprint | `[start_px + 96, start_px + W·48) × [line_px, line_px + 24)` | `[start_px, start_px + leaf_w) × [line_px, line_px + 24)` |

Checks against the fixtures: `fixture_airlock` (E, `line_px` 696, `start_px` 240, `W` 2) gives footprint `[672, 696) × [240, 336)` with no JAMB; `fixture_derelict_b_socket` (W, `line_px` 120, `start_px` 144) gives `[120, 144) × [144, 240)`; `fixture_ns_pair` host (S, `line_px` 480) gives `[456, 480)` and donor (N, `line_px` 96) gives `[96, 120)`, which land abutting at body `y` 480 (AC-68). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

*Socket economy — flagged, not solved.* With one home-ship socket and a terminal `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN`, the first weld-then-cut leaves the ship with no free socket for the rest of the MVP slice. This is acceptable for the MVP slice (one weld scenario, concept MVP definition) and recorded as a Vertical Slice question to Modular Ship Assembly and the game-designer: either more sockets per home-ship, or a verb that re-cuts a `CAPPED` socket open again while leaving its history visible (old bead plus cut ring). The three options and the socket-economy formula are in Open Questions. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Consequence for the fantasy and the experience targets:** with one socket and one mate there is no *choice* of what to weld (only whether), so the claim that the crew chooses *what* to graft (Player Fantasy, X-3) is a Vertical Slice claim; and if OQ-1 is resolved before then, the design review's preferred answer is **option A** (a re-cut verb that reopens a `CAPPED` socket while leaving its history visible), because it is the only option that does not delete the scar the fantasy is built on.

**LY-14 — The mating predicate, `socket_plan` and `can_attach`.** Two sockets MATE iff all of the following hold; the verdict is the FIRST failing reason in this order (cheap before expensive; closed set, distinct from the Graph's): both exist (`SOCKET_UNKNOWN`); both are `FREE` (`SOCKET_NOT_FREE`); they lie on different bodies (`SAME_BODY`); facings are opposite (`FACING_MISMATCH`); `width_tiles` equal (`WIDTH_MISMATCH`); classes compatible (`CLASS_MISMATCH`; MVP: equal `class_id`); lane multisets equal by `(loop, lane_index)` (`LANE_MISMATCH`); and the translated footprints of the two bodies do not overlap (`GEOM_OVERLAP`, D.2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The `GEOM_OVERLAP` test set is the STATIC footprint, not `rects_in`:** `rects_in` returns occluders in their current leaf state, so a low prop (SOLID, not occluding) would escape it, the verdict would flip as a door animates, and floor laid on floor would pass. The test therefore runs over (i) every static rect of both bodies with **all** flags (SOLID or not, occluding or not), each socket's PLATE slot counted at its full footprint (the maximal, FREE-state geometry) and no leaf or JAMB slot, (ii) the tile cells of every room of both bodies (rect against tile, and tile against tile, so a wall over the other body's floor and two floors on one cell are both `GEOM_OVERLAP`), after the D.6 translation; abutting is legal. It uses the broadphase grid of each body and is **memoised on `(socket_a, socket_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)`** (D.22), so a door animating on either body never invalidates or flips it. The mated PLATE footprints of the two sockets themselves abut at the seam line and do not overlap. **Order of the two verdicts (C-4):** Layout's `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` answers socket-level occupancy FIRST; the Graph's `SOCKET_OCCUPIED` (LSG:170) remains the port- and edge-level reason. Because `SAME_BODY` is a hard reject and every weld merges two bodies, the weld relation over sections is always a forest, so a cut always splits a body into exactly two components (no ring, no "cut that does not split").
*Geometry.* Mating is ABUT: the two 24-px hull walls sit side by side, the shared boundary is the seam line and the door frames are in line. The weld offset is `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a − pos_b` (D.6). Every input of that sum lies on the 24-px grid (lint `GRID_24`, LY-30) and `offset_a` does too, so `offset_b` lies on the 24-px grid by construction (D.6): the closure needs no catalogue-wide socket phase, because rooms sit on per-room 24-px origins (LY-5). Any off-grid `offset_b` from a validated plan is a defect, not a reason code. The N/S double bulkhead's up-screen face arrangement is routed to the art-director (PIPE:794), not a Layout rule.
*`socket_plan(socket_a, socket_b) -> {pairs[], openings[], L_seam, reason}`* is a PURE query returning the Graph's weld-plan DATA verbatim (LSG:170): `pairs[]` one per lane, `openings[]` one per mated hatch pair `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)`, `L_seam = width_tiles`. **Assembly adds `q` and issues the command; the Graph's `can_join(plan)` validates; both verdicts must pass before `apply`** *(Modular Ship Assembly is designed; MSA repeats this)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* This is the whole answer to the index's "three GDDs would each define a socket" (IDX:28): one record type, one mating rule, one plan builder. Lane matching is by `(loop, lane_index)` (positional within the socket), so a pipe never visibly kinks across the seam. A socket with no `hatch` is bulkhead-only (the weld joins lanes only; `openings[]` is empty). *(CLARIFY, orchestrator ruling: one-sided hatches.)* If exactly one of two mating sockets declares a hatch, the pair is legal and behaves as bulkhead-only: `openings[]` is empty, the hatched socket's hatch stays HULL (its PLATE slot stays active, as in `FREE`, LY-15) while the socket is `WELDED`, `socket_plan` raises the diagnostic `hatch_one_sided`, and no reason code is added (the closed set of LY-29 stands). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The player must be able to read it before the weld spends the socket:** `hatch_one_sided` is part of the `can_attach` / `socket_plan` **preview payload** `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}`, and the weld cursor outline (UI Requirements) shows the one-sided side diegetically as a closed bulkhead outline with no hatch ring on the bare side — "no passage here" — so welding onto a hatchless mate is never a surprise (routed to Modular Ship Assembly and the art-director). Rejected: a mismatch reason (it would forbid welding a hatched home-ship dock to a derelict whose wreck lost its hatch, which is the common case) and an automatic hatch on the bare side (Layout never invents geometry). A hatch requires `width_tiles >= 2` and is **low-aligned**: its `doorway_start_px` equals the socket's `start_px` (lint `HATCH_WIDTH` checks the width and lint `HATCH_ALIGN` checks the alignment; the field is derived for a hatch door and any other authored value is the lint error `HATCH_ALIGN`). A 3-tile (144-px) socket holds one 96-px hatch plus 48 px of bulkhead on the HIGH side. Low alignment is what keeps the two hatches of a mate in line: spans coincide after the D.6 translation and "LOW" is the same side in both frames (LY-9), so no per-hatch offset can differ and no `HATCH_OFFSET_MISMATCH` lint is needed. Both MVP fixtures satisfy it (`fixture_airlock`: `doorway_start_px` 240 = `start_px` 240; `fixture_derelict_b_socket`: 144 = 144). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

1122	Status vocabulary: **designed** (a complete GDD on disk), **in-flight** (being designed concurrently in this run; no complete GDD on disk, at most a draft or a stage brief), **undesigned-provisional** (no file and no stage in this run; every contract is provisional). "Hard" means the dependent cannot function without the interface; "soft" means it degrades.
1123

449	**LY-31 — The PROJECTOR contract.** Layout's data module is scene-tree free (kernel H10): a headless test asserts it references no `Node`. A **separate PROJECTOR** (subscriber class `PROJECTOR`, CR-10: "write engine-side *derived* objects owned by its block owner … never writes blocks"; kernel example "Layout → physics projection; derelict content build") builds engine-side derived objects from `layout.state` and the templates; they are never persisted and are rebuilt from the block, also after restore. The object shape (the [UNV] default and the weld spike that measures it) is in the engine feasibility note and ADR-LAY-03, not in this contract. It builds the door, prop and machinery sprites from the rect table and the seam bead, cap plate and scar pieces from `welds[]` and socket state. It fills the Pipeline's PR-5 layer stack (floor z 0 never Y-sorted, floor marks, ONE Y-sort `Node2D` holding in tree order wall-face, wall-mounted, doors, props, machinery, actors; wall caps) and gives every placed SPRITE object (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead or plate piece) the Pipeline's **`entity_id`** (PIPE D.12, PIPE:553: persistent, owned by the state block, stable across save and reload; the third key of `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`, PIPE:1139). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `creation_id` is retired; the Pipeline has no such field.)* **Layout's `entity_id` (publisher-defined, G1; the namespace tag is registered with the Pipeline, Open Questions OQ-LY-ID):** a block-tagged int64, `entity_id = (LAYOUT_ID_NS << 56) | (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | template_local_idx`, with `LAYOUT_ID_NS` a Layout namespace byte in `1 … 127` (GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit, so a byte of 128 or more would make every Layout `entity_id` negative; the Pipeline compares ids as plain ints and only relative order inside one namespace matters, but the range is fixed so the sign is never in question) that Body, Interaction and any other id publisher must not use in its own high bits (so a Layout id can never equal a Body or Interaction id in the same `class_rank`), `section_id` 32 bits at most (`next_section_id` is monotonic and tombstones keep their ids), `kind_ordinal` 8 bits, `template_local_idx` 16 bits. It is a pure function of the block (`section_id`) and the template, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one, and it is never persisted by the PROJECTOR. **Tiles carry no `entity_id`:** `TileMapLayer` cells are not nodes; wall-face and cap tiles are `class_rank` 0 and tie-break among themselves by cell position `(y, x)` (the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`, Y-sort mechanism per SP-YSORT-1 below). Within `class_rank` 2 the doors, props and machinery of one `sort_y` are ordered by `entity_id` alone (they share one rank in the Pipeline; Layout assumes no sub-rank). The *mechanism* that delivers the key (`TileMapLayer` participation, who owns child insertion order) is not defined here and stays gated on SP-YSORT-1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* It writes no block and creates **no engine tile collision and no navigation mesh in MVP**. It never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D` (Lighting's). Its section nodes are parented under Body's per-body root `Node2D` (Body's `body.projector` owns the root and its translation, BDY-33) — the default shape, which the Y-sort spike below may supersede with option B (no reparent; BDY-33 would then own the pose-driven section positions rather than a root). (→ ADR-LAY-03.) The PROJECTOR must satisfy "never hidden" (art bible 6.1) for seam beads. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Prerequisite story — the Y-sort / PROJECTOR scene-shape spike (SP-YSORT-1), done before the PROJECTOR story starts.** The default shape above reparents section nodes under a per-body root on every weld, which sits badly with the Pipeline's single Y-sort scope (PR-5: ONE Y-sort `Node2D` holding wall-face, wall-mounted, doors, props, machinery and actors in tree order) and is [UNV]. The spike tests **option B first**: *no reparent* — every section's nodes keep one parent under the single Y-sort node and each section's position is driven from the body's pose plus `section_offset` every tick (so a weld changes an offset, never a parent) — and falls back to option A (per-body roots, reparent on weld) only if B fails. **Exit criteria:** (1) the PR-5 draw order of AC-123 holds with two bodies in one scene and across a weld (an actor south of a wall over its face, north of it behind it, the cap above both); (2) no sprite changes sort rank across the weld frame; (3) draw calls for the MVP world are recorded for both options; (4) the weld frame costs at most one frame over the P99 ceiling (16.6 ms on RM-DESKTOP, 33.3 ms on RM-DECK; pending spike measurement) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*; (5) the result is written to ADR-LAY-03. Each run **records the machine specification, the startup read-back and the measured P99 and mean as retained evidence** (`production/qa/evidence/layout-perf-<criterion>-<machine>.md`; a measurement from the developer's machine is indicative only, never a pass). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* If a measured rung misses its line, the fallback ladder of D.22 is climbed one data-layout step at a time; a GDExtension or C# rung needs technical-director sign-off. The cases cover D.22's terms: a single actor, **8 aggregate actors per tick**, and an **Emitter-sized query** (a 288 × 288 px box). Every measurement uses a Godot 4.7.2 release export, not the editor-debug build, a warm-up of 100 calls (CPU-only micro-probes; render-dependent rows use the pipeline's 120-frame warm-up), and at least 10,000 calls (or 600 ticks × 2 actors).

Gated on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, pending spike measurement. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*

# TRs: Ship Section & Layout Data Model (alias: section)

Source: design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-section-001 | Layout registers exactly one kernel state block `layout.state` (class SIM, persist true, persist_scope WORLD, scope SHARED, schema_version 1, `restore_after: []`, one hook `layout.doors`) with callbacks snapshot/restore/default_state/post_restore/read_view. | Core | LY-1 |
| TR-section-002 | The Layout data module is scene-tree free and integer-only: a headless test must assert it references no `Node` and no float exists in any Layout value. | Core | LY-3 a, LY-31 (kernel H10) |
| TR-section-003 | Templates (rooms, tiles, rect table, doors, sockets, hardpoints, slots, anchors) are immutable data loaded in BOOTING from a committed `assets/data/sections/manifest.json` in sorted `template_id` order (never a DirAccess scan), never appear in a snapshot, and every JSON number is int-cast and bound-checked. | Data | LY-2 |
| TR-section-004 | `layout.state` stores instances by reference to templates (bodies table, 13-int section-instance rows, sparse non-FREE socket table, `welds[]`, counters `next_section_id`/`next_body_id`/`next_room_id`); derived caches (broadphase grid, leaf rects, version counters, `opening_leaves`, `graph_ref` maps) are never persisted. | Save/Load | LY-2, D.21 |
| TR-section-005 | Ids (`section_id`, `body_id`, `room_id`) are allocated by Layout from persisted counters in template order, never reused or renumbered; a discarded section remains a tombstone row; `graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` is persisted per instance. | Save/Load | LY-6, LY-19 |
| TR-section-006 | Snapshot encoding uses dense parallel packed arrays in ascending id order (no int-keyed Dictionary, no Vector2i/Rect2/Resource), 64-bit values (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`) as two 32-bit halves, and `snapshot()` returns deep copies. | Save/Load | LY-26 a |
| TR-section-007 | `restore()` swaps whole tables from scratch only on success, rejects unsupported stored_version, unknown `template_id`, structural template change, or geometry_hash change on an instance with history; `rot_q != 0` is rejected (`LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`). | Save/Load | LY-26 a/e, LY-3 d |
| TR-section-008 | Static queries (room_at, V, exposed_tiles, section_offset, body_of, socket_plan, static rects) are valid immediately after `restore()`; leaf-dependent queries are valid only after Layout's `post_restore()` (derive_doors pass) and report template-default closed leaves with a `stale_leaf` diagnostic before it. | Save/Load | LY-26 b/c |
| TR-section-009 | `post_restore()` performs cross-block verification only (graph_ref_base resolves, def_ids resolve, weld seam_ids resolve in Graph) and rebuilds `opening_leaves`, bumping version/leaf_version for sections with open leaves. | Save/Load | LY-26 c/d |
| TR-section-010 | Geometry is expressed as half-open integer rects `[x0,x1)x[y0,y1)` in base px with a flags byte (SOLID, OCCLUDES_LIGHT, DOOR_LEAF, PROP, MACHINE, HULL) on a 24-px grid (TILE_PX 48, WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH 24); px-to-tile conversion uses floor division, and transforms are integer translation only (no rotation, mirror or zoom value). | Core | LY-3, LY-7, D.1 |
| TR-section-011 | One rect set serves collision (Body `solid_in`), light occlusion (Emitter/Lighting `rects_in`) and drawing, with no "perceived" or phantom variant of any query; the avatar has no engine physics body and no engine tile collision or navigation mesh is created. | Physics | LY-7, LY-31, LY-34 (Pillar 1) |

- Registry entries: `layout_rect_flags`, `socket_state`, `mvp_template_roster`, `layout_state_block`; retires `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM`.
- Data: template schema `SECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1, `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1, `assets/data/sections/manifest.json`, `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json`.

- Item & Module Database: `compatible_defs(hardpoint)` (F-6), `MAX_PORTS_PER_DEF`, `fresh_instance` (via Authoring/Interaction).
- Save/Load: SL-2 type rules, SL-14 migration, SL-18 `init_world` (caller), `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`.
- Web Map & Transit: sole caller of LM1/LM4 (`init_world`).
- Modular Ship Assembly: caller of LM2/LM3; supplies `q`.

- Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline: PR-5 layer stack, Y-sort key D.12 `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`.
- Emitter State / Lighting / Failure & Trail / Suit / Adaptive Audio / Instruments / Horror / Perception Filter: downstream readers (Layout supplies reads).
- Art bible 6.3 / 8.2 kit and door cell (authoring input).

## Engine risk

- Packed arrays (PackedInt64Array/PackedInt32Array/PackedByteArray) with the 4.7 element-write change (no whole-property setter call): HIGH (explicit dirty tracking mandated).
- 4.7 typed-return override change (override of typed-return method needs explicit return; matters for abstract `OccluderSource`): HIGH.
- `@abstract` (4.5) for the `OccluderSource` seam (verify before use): HIGH.
- `TileMapLayer` per-section/per-body batching, Y-sort under reparent, rotation/collision/nav in 4.6/4.7 (spike SP-YSORT-1, ADR-LAY-03): HIGH (batching/Y-sort tie rule [UNV]), MEDIUM (rotation/collision/nav, unused).
- Y-sorting via `Node2D` with y_sort_enabled and tree-order tie rule: MEDIUM/HIGH ([UNV]; mitigated by Pipeline `entity_id` key).
- `var_to_bytes` determinism and typed-container snapshot encoding [UNV]: MEDIUM.
- GDScript cost of `rects_in`/`solid_in` over ~2,000 rects, `PackedArray.resize` cost (spike SP-ENG-1, AC-136/164/137): MEDIUM.
- JSON parser returns floats (int-cast required) and export-build non-resource file filtering (`include_filter` for `*.json`), DirAccess order is platform-dependent: LOW.
- Release export template, forward_plus renderer, vsync for measurement builds: LOW.
- No Light2D/LightOccluder2D, no engine physics shapes, no NavigationServer used by Layout: none.

# TRs: Ship Section & Layout Data Model (alias: section)

Source: design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-section-001 | Layout registers exactly one kernel state block `layout.state` (class SIM, persist true, persist_scope WORLD, scope SHARED, schema_version 1, `restore_after: []`, one hook `layout.doors`) with callbacks snapshot/restore/default_state/post_restore/read_view. | Core | LY-1 |
| TR-section-002 | The Layout data module is scene-tree free and integer-only: a headless test must assert it references no `Node` and no float exists in any Layout value. | Core | LY-3 a, LY-31 (kernel H10) |
| TR-section-003 | Templates (rooms, tiles, rect table, doors, sockets, hardpoints, slots, anchors) are immutable data loaded in BOOTING from a committed `assets/data/sections/manifest.json` in sorted `template_id` order (never a DirAccess scan), never appear in a snapshot, and every JSON number is int-cast and bound-checked. | Data | LY-2 |
| TR-section-004 | `layout.state` stores instances by reference to templates (bodies table, 13-int section-instance rows, sparse non-FREE socket table, `welds[]`, counters `next_section_id`/`next_body_id`/`next_room_id`); derived caches (broadphase grid, leaf rects, version counters, `opening_leaves`, `graph_ref` maps) are never persisted. | Save/Load | LY-2, D.21 |
| TR-section-005 | Ids (`section_id`, `body_id`, `room_id`) are allocated by Layout from persisted counters in template order, never reused or renumbered; a discarded section remains a tombstone row; `graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` is persisted per instance. | Save/Load | LY-6, LY-19 |
| TR-section-006 | Snapshot encoding uses dense parallel packed arrays in ascending id order (no int-keyed Dictionary, no Vector2i/Rect2/Resource), 64-bit values (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`) as two 32-bit halves, and `snapshot()` returns deep copies. | Save/Load | LY-26 a |
| TR-section-007 | `restore()` swaps whole tables from scratch only on success, rejects unsupported stored_version, unknown `template_id`, structural template change, or geometry_hash change on an instance with history; `rot_q != 0` is rejected (`LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`). | Save/Load | LY-26 a/e, LY-3 d |
| TR-section-008 | Static queries (room_at, V, exposed_tiles, section_offset, body_of, socket_plan, static rects) are valid immediately after `restore()`; leaf-dependent queries are valid only after Layout's `post_restore()` (derive_doors pass) and report template-default closed leaves with a `stale_leaf` diagnostic before it. | Save/Load | LY-26 b/c |
| TR-section-009 | `post_restore()` performs cross-block verification only (graph_ref_base resolves, def_ids resolve, weld seam_ids resolve in Graph) and rebuilds `opening_leaves`, bumping version/leaf_version for sections with open leaves. | Save/Load | LY-26 c/d |
| TR-section-010 | Geometry is expressed as half-open integer rects `[x0,x1)x[y0,y1)` in base px with a flags byte (SOLID, OCCLUDES_LIGHT, DOOR_LEAF, PROP, MACHINE, HULL) on a 24-px grid (TILE_PX 48, WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH 24); px-to-tile conversion uses floor division, and transforms are integer translation only (no rotation, mirror or zoom value). | Core | LY-3, LY-7, D.1 |
| TR-section-011 | One rect set serves collision (Body `solid_in`), light occlusion (Emitter/Lighting `rects_in`) and drawing, with no "perceived" or phantom variant of any query; the avatar has no engine physics body and no engine tile collision or navigation mesh is created. | Physics | LY-7, LY-31, LY-34 (Pillar 1) |
| TR-section-012 | `layout.doors` hook (divisor 1, `after: []`) runs in P3, re-derives each door/hatch leaf rect from the Graph's `opening(edge_id) -> {area, area_max, door_state}` with `leaf_w = width_px - floor(width_px*area/area_max)`, and bumps leaf_version/version once per changed section; `body.integrate` is `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`. | Threading/Timing | LY-9, LY-10 |
| TR-section-013 | Layout never stores, mirrors or writes `area` or `door_state`; every template-door/hatch `area` write must occur in P2 via command (never M13 from a P3 hook), and the door leaf sprite extent must equal the leaf rect (no tween). | Core | LY-10, LY-11, LY-35 |
| TR-section-014 | `leaf_would_overlap(opening_ref=Graph edge_id, area, foot_boxes[])` and `leaf_obstruction` are pure queries evaluating every leaf of the opening (both sections of a mated hatch); foot boxes are caller-supplied arguments and Layout reads nothing from `body.state`. | Core | LY-11 |
| TR-section-015 | Hot-path `rects_in(aabb, out)` / `solid_in(body_id, aabb, out)` fill a caller-owned QueryBuffer (PackedInt64Array keys `section_id*RECT_KEY_STRIDE+idx`, PackedInt32Array occupied spans `(x0,y0,x1-1,y1-1)`, PackedByteArray flags) in ascending key order and allocate nothing in steady state (0 bytes growth over 9,000 calls). | Performance | LY-12 e, AC-137 |
| TR-section-016 | A per-body derived uniform-grid broadphase (BROADPHASE_CELL_PX 48, never persisted, rebuilt at build/attach/detach/restore) answers `solid_in` at P99 <= 0.05 ms per actor with a 2,000-rect body (aggregate 8 actors <= 0.6 ms; Emitter 288x288 query <= 0.3 ms) on RM-DESKTOP/RM-DECK release export. | Performance | LY-12 c, D.22, AC-136, AC-164 |
| TR-section-017 | Per-section `version`, `static_version`, `leaf_version` are monotone, non-persisted, reset to 1 on restore, and bumped for every section whose rect set can change (both sections of a weld/cut including the unmoved host, and every moved section); `changed_region(section_id) -> ALL|REGION|FRAME` is valid only for the current tick. | Core | LY-12 d |
| TR-section-018 | Sockets are pre-declared attachment sites with states FREE -> WELDED(seam_id) -> CAPPED or CUT_OPEN, which never return to FREE in MVP; sockets change state only inside LM2/LM3 (no `install_cap_plate` or `set_socket_state` mutator). | Core | LY-13, LY-27 |
| TR-section-019 | `can_attach` applies a fixed first-failure-wins reason order (SOCKET_UNKNOWN, SOCKET_NOT_FREE, SAME_BODY, FACING_MISMATCH, WIDTH_MISMATCH, CLASS_MISMATCH, LANE_MISMATCH, GEOM_OVERLAP) with GEOM_OVERLAP tested over static footprints and tile cells, memoised on (socket_a, socket_b, static_version_a, static_version_b), <= 2 ms uncached. | Core | LY-14, AC-138 |

| TR-section-022 | Dirty tracking is explicit inside each mutator (not via packed-array property setters, due to the Godot 4.7 packed-array element-write change); dirty keys are ints `(KIND<<32)|id` (SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3), batched to the PROJECTOR subscriber, collapsing to ALL past MAX_DIRTY_KEYS 256. | Core | LY-27, LY-32 |
